Commentary of Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Quran al-'Azim) on surah 27, verse 1–6:

Surah al-Naml

It is a Meccan surah.

In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

* *

The discussion of the muqatta'at (the disjointed letters) at the beginnings of surahs has already been presented in Surat al-Baqarah.

* *

His saying: ﴿These are the verses of the Qur'an and a Book that makes things clear﴾, meaning: these are the verses of the Qur'an and a Book that is clear and evident.

﴿A guidance and good tidings for the believers﴾, meaning: guidance and glad tidings come from the Qur'an only to those who believe in it, follow it, affirm it, act upon what is in it, establish the obligatory prayer, give the obligatory zakah, and have certain faith in the Last Abode, the resurrection after death, the recompense for deeds, good and evil, and Paradise and Hellfire. As Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿Say, it is for those who believe a guidance and a healing; and as for those who do not believe, there is deafness in their ears, and it is blindness for them. Those are being called from a distant place﴾ [Fussilat: 44]. And He said: ﴿So that you may give good tidings thereby to the righteous and warn thereby a people contentious﴾ [Maryam: 97]. Therefore He says here: ﴿Indeed, those who do not believe in the Hereafter﴾, meaning: they deny it and consider its occurrence far-fetched, ﴿We have made attractive to them their deeds, so they wander bewildered﴾, meaning: We made beautiful to them what they are engaged in, and We extended them in their transgression, so they wander bewildered in their error. This was a recompense for their denial of the Last Abode, as Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿And We turn their hearts and their sights away, as they did not believe in it the first time, and We leave them in their transgression, wandering bewildered﴾ [al-An'am: 110]. ﴿Those are the ones for whom is the worst of punishment﴾, meaning: in this world and the Hereafter. ﴿And they in the Hereafter are the greatest losers﴾, meaning: none loses his soul and his wealth except them, among the people of the gathering place.

* *

His saying: ﴿And indeed, you are receiving the Qur'an from the Wise, the Knowing﴾, meaning: ﴿And indeed, you﴾, O Muhammad. Qatadah said: ﴿tulaqqa﴾ means "you are taking." ﴿The Qur'an from the Wise, the Knowing﴾, meaning: from the presence of One who is Wise, Knowing, that is, Wise in His commands and prohibitions, Knowing of matters both great and small. So His report is pure truth, and His judgment is perfect justice, as Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿And the word of your Lord has been fulfilled in truth and justice; none can alter His words﴾ [al-An'am: 115].

* *

His saying: ﴿And indeed, you are receiving the Qur'an from the Wise, the Knowing﴾, meaning: ﴿And indeed, you﴾, O Muhammad. Qatadah said: ﴿tulaqqa﴾ means "you are taking." ﴿The Qur'an from the Wise, the Knowing﴾, meaning: from the presence of One who is Wise, Knowing, that is, Wise in His commands and prohibitions, Knowing of matters both great and small. So His report is pure truth, and His judgment is perfect justice, as Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿And the word of your Lord has been fulfilled in truth and justice; none can alter His words﴾ [al-An'am: 115].

Ibn Kathir said, addressing His Messenger (ﷺ), reminding him of the matter of Musa (Moses): how Allah chose him, spoke to him, conversed with him, and gave him great, dazzling signs and compelling proofs, and sent him to Fir'awn (Pharaoh) and his chiefs. But they denied them, disbelieved, and were arrogant toward following him and submitting to him. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿When Musa said to his family﴾, meaning: remember when Musa traveled with his family, lost his way, and that was in the night and darkness. Then he perceived from the side of the Mount a fire, meaning he saw a fire blazing and flaring up, and he said: ﴿to his family, "Indeed, I have perceived a fire. I will bring you from it news"﴾, meaning about the way, ﴿"or bring you a burning brand so that you may warm yourselves"﴾, meaning, so that you may warm yourselves by it. It happened as he said: he returned from it with a great report and took from it a great light. Therefore Allah the Exalted said: ﴿So when he came to it, he was called, "Blessed is whoever is in the fire and whoever is around it"﴾, meaning: when he came to it, he saw a tremendous, awesome sight, as he reached it, and the fire was blazing in a green tree, the fire not increasing except in intensity, and the tree not increasing except in greenery and freshness. Then he raised his head, and behold, its light was connected to the horizon of the sky.

Ibn 'Abbas and others said: it was not fire; it was only light blazing.

In a narration from Ibn 'Abbas: it was the light of the Lord of the worlds. So Musa stood, amazed at what he saw, and he was called: "Blessed is whoever is in the fire." Ibn 'Abbas said: [i.e.] it was sanctified.

﴿And whoever is around it﴾, meaning: from among the angels. This was said by Ibn 'Abbas, 'Ikrimah, Sa'id ibn Jubayr, al-Hasan, and Qatadah.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Yunus ibn Habib narrated to us, Abu Dawud — that is al-Tayalisi — narrated to us, Shu'bah and al-Mas'udi narrated to us, from 'Amr ibn Murrah, who heard Abu 'Ubaydah narrating, from Abu Musa, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Indeed Allah does not sleep, nor is it fitting for Him to sleep. He lowers the scale and raises it. The deeds of the night are raised to Him before the day, and the deeds of the day before the night." Al-Mas'udi added: "His veil is light — or fire — and if He were to uncover it, the splendors of His face would burn everything that His sight reaches." Then Abu 'Ubaydah recited: ﴿that blessed is whoever is in the fire and whoever is around it﴾. [Ahmad narrated it in his Musnad (4/401) through Waki' from al-Mas'udi with similar wording.] The origin of this hadith is recorded in Sahih Muslim, from the hadith of 'Amr ibn Murrah, with it.

As for His saying: ﴿And exalted is Allah, Lord of the worlds﴾, meaning: He who does what He wills, who does not resemble any of His creations, and whom none of His made things can encompass. He is the Most High, the Mighty, distinct from all creation, neither the earth nor the heavens enclose Him. Rather, He is the One, the Eternal Refuge, exempt from likeness to originated things.

As for His saying: ﴿O Musa, indeed I am Allah, the Mighty, the Wise﴾, He informed him that the One who addresses him and converses with him is his Lord, Allah, the Mighty, who overpowers, subdues, and defeats everything, the Wise in His actions and words.

Then He commanded him to cast his staff from his hand, to show him a clear proof that He is the doer who chooses, able over all things. When Musa cast that staff from his hand, it instantly turned into a great, fearsome serpent, extremely large and yet very swift in motion. Therefore He said: ﴿But when he saw it moving as if it were a jann﴾. The jann is a kind of snake, the swiftest in movement and the most agitated. (In a hadith there is a prohibition against killing the jinn of the houses [a reference to house snakes] [Sahih al-Bukhari no. 3298, from the hadith of Ibn 'Umar, may Allah be pleased with them both].) When Musa saw that, ﴿he turned back fleeing and did not return﴾, meaning he did not look back out of extreme fear. ﴿O Musa, do not fear. Indeed, the messengers do not fear in My presence﴾, meaning: do not fear what you see, for I intend to choose you as a messenger and make you a prophet of high station.

As for His saying: ﴿Except for one who has wronged and then substituted good after evil — indeed, I am Forgiving and Merciful﴾, this is a disjunctive exception, and in it is a great glad tiding for mankind: whoever was upon something [of wrongdoing] and then gave it up, returned and repented, Allah will turn to him in forgiveness, as He said: ﴿And indeed, I am the Forgiving of whoever repents, believes, does righteousness, and then remains guided﴾ [Ta-Ha: 82], and He said: ﴿And whoever does evil or wrongs himself and then seeks Allah's forgiveness will find Allah Forgiving and Merciful﴾ [An-Nisa': 110]. The verses on this are very numerous.

As for His saying: ﴿And put your hand into your bosom; it will come out white without disease﴾, this is another sign and a dazzling proof of the power of Allah, the Doer who chooses, and of the truthfulness of the one to whom He gave a miracle. Allah the Exalted commanded him to put his hand into the opening of his garment; when he put it in and took it out, it came out white, radiant, as if it were a piece of the moon, with a gleam flashing like lightning.

As for His saying: ﴿among nine signs﴾, meaning: these two are two of nine signs with which I support you, and I make them a proof for you to Fir'awn and his people. ﴿Indeed, they were a defiant people.﴾

These are the nine signs which Allah the Exalted mentioned: ﴿And We certainly gave Musa nine clear signs﴾ [Al-Isra': 101], as has already been explained there.

As for His saying: ﴿But when Our signs came to them as eye-opening, they said, "This is clear magic"﴾, meaning: clear, evident, and manifest. They wanted to oppose him with their magic, but they were overcome there, ﴿and they turned back humiliated﴾.

﴿And they denied them﴾, meaning outwardly, ﴿though their souls were convinced of them﴾, meaning they knew within themselves that they were true from Allah, but they denied them, opposed them, and were arrogant toward them, ﴿out of wrongdoing and arrogance﴾, meaning wrongdoing from themselves, a cursed disposition, ﴿and arrogance﴾, meaning pride against following the truth. Therefore He said: ﴿So see how was the end of the corrupters﴾, meaning: look, O Muhammad, at how the outcome of their disbelief was, in Allah's destruction of them and their drowning, all of them, in a single morning.

The implied address says: Beware, O you who deny Muhammad and reject what he has brought from his Lord, lest there befall you what befell them, by way of greater priority and fitness. For Muhammad (ﷺ) is more noble and greater than Musa, and his proof is more manifest and stronger than the proof of Musa, by the proofs that Allah gave him, joined to his own existence and character, and by the glad tidings of him that preceded from the prophets, and by the covenants taken for him from his Lord, may the best of prayers and peace be upon him.

Ibn Kathir, *Tafsir al-Qur'an al-'Azim*, on Surah 27, verses 15–19:

God Most High informs us of the great blessings, the magnificent gifts, and the noble qualities with which He favored His two servants and prophets, Dawud (David) and his son Sulayman (Solomon), upon them be peace from God. He combined for them the happiness of this world and the Hereafter, kingship and complete authority in this world, and prophethood and messengership in the religion. For this reason He said: ﴿And We gave David and Solomon knowledge, and they said, "Praise be to God, who has favored us over many of His believing servants."﴾

Ibn Abi Hatim said: It was related from Ibrahim ibn Yahya ibn Tamam [in one manuscript: "Hisham"]: my father informed me, from my grandfather, who said: 'Umar ibn 'Abd al-'Aziz wrote: "God does not bestow a blessing upon a servant and then the servant praises God for it, except that his praise is better than His blessing, even if you knew this only from the Book of God that was revealed; God said: ﴿And We gave David and Solomon knowledge, and they said, 'Praise be to God, who has favored us over many of His believing servants.'﴾ And what blessing is greater than what was given to David and Solomon, upon them be peace?"

* *

His saying: ﴿And Solomon inherited from David﴾ means in kingship and prophethood. The intended meaning is not the inheritance of wealth, for if it were so, He would not have singled out Solomon alone from among David's other children, since David had a hundred wives. Rather, what is meant is the inheritance of kingship and prophethood, because the property of the prophets is not inherited, as the Messenger of God (ﷺ) informed us in his saying: "We, the company of prophets, do not leave inheritance; what we leave is charity." [Related by al-Bukhari in his Sahih, no. 6727, from 'A'ishah, with the wording: "We do not leave inheritance; what we leave is charity." The hafiz Ibn Hajar said in al-Fath (12/8): "As for what is famous in the books of the jurists and others with the wording 'We, the company of prophets, do not leave inheritance,' a group of the imams denied it, and this is so specifically regarding the exact wording 'we' (nahnu). See the rest of his discussion and his interpretation of the meaning of the hadith in al-Fath."]

* *

His saying: ﴿"O people, we have been taught the speech of birds, and we have been given of everything"﴾ means: Solomon informed of the blessings of God upon him, in what He granted him of complete kingship and great authority, to the extent that He subjected to him mankind, the jinn, and the birds. He also understood the language of birds and animals, and this is something that, as far as we know from what God and His Messenger have informed us, no one among mankind was given. As for the claim of some ignorant and vulgar people that animals used to speak like the children of Adam before Solomon son of David, as many people utter, it is speech without knowledge. Had the matter been so, there would be no point in singling out Solomon for this, since everyone hears the speech of birds and beasts and understands what they say. The matter is not as they claim or say; rather, animals, birds, and all other creatures have remained in this form and manner from the time they were created until our present time. But God, glorified and exalted, had made Solomon, upon him be peace, understand what birds say to one another in the air, and what the various kinds of animals speak. For this reason He said: ﴿"We have been taught the speech of birds, and we have been given of everything"﴾, meaning of what a king needs; ﴿"Indeed, this is the manifest bounty"﴾, meaning the clear and evident favor of God upon us.

Imam Ahmad said: Qutaybah related to us, Ya'qub ibn 'Abd al-Rahman related to us, from 'Amr ibn Abi 'Amr, from al-Muttalib, from Abu Hurayrah, may God be pleased with him, that the Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "David, upon him be peace, had intense jealousy, so whenever he went out, the doors were locked, and no one would enter upon his family until he returned." He said: "One day he went out, and the doors were locked, and his wife came forward to look toward the house, and there was a man standing in the middle of the house. She said to those in the house: 'From where did this man enter, while the house is locked? By God, we will be disgraced because of David!' David, upon him be peace, came, and there was the man standing in the middle of the house. David said to him: 'Who are you?' He said: 'One who does not fear kings, and is not kept back by chamberlains.' David said: 'Then by God, you are the Angel of Death. Welcome, by the command of God.' So David, upon him be peace, remained in his place until his soul was taken, until his affair was finished and the sun rose upon him. Then Solomon, upon him be peace, said to the birds: 'Shade David!' So the birds shaded him until the earth was darkened over them both. Then Solomon said to them: 'Fold your wings one by one.'" Abu Hurayrah said: "O Messenger of God, how did the birds do it?" So the Messenger of God (ﷺ) closed his hand, and on that day the *mudrahiyyah* overcame him. [Al-Musnad (2/419). Al-Haythami said in al-Majma' (8/206): "In it is al-Muttalib ibn 'Abd Allah ibn Hanatab, whom Abu Zur'ah and others declared trustworthy, and the rest of its narrators are narrators of the Sahih."]

Abu al-Faraj ibn al-Jawzi said: *al-Mudrahiyyah* (المضرحية) [in the manuscripts: "al-Mus.rahiyyah," and the version adopted from Lisan al-'Arab, entry "d-r-h"] means the red vultures.

* *

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And there were gathered for Solomon his hosts of jinn and men and birds, and they were marshaled in ranks﴾ means: his hosts were assembled for Solomon from the jinn, the men, and the birds, meaning that he rode among them in great pomp and majesty. Among mankind were those closest to him, the jinn came next in rank, and the birds had their station above his head, so that if the sun was hot, they shaded him with their wings.

* *

His saying: ﴿So they were marshaled in ranks﴾ means: the first of them was held back to the last of them, so that no one would advance beyond his proper station, which was assigned to him.

Mujahid said: He appointed over each kind guards who turned back its first members to its last, so that they would not advance ahead during the march, as kings do today.

* *

His saying: ﴿Until, when they came upon the valley of the ants﴾ means: until, when Solomon, upon him be peace, passed with those of the armies and hosts who were with him, upon the valley of the ants, ﴿a female ant said, "O ants, enter your dwellings, lest Solomon and his hosts crush you while they do not perceive."﴾

Ibn 'Asakir related, by way of Ishaq ibn Bishr, from Sa'id, from Qatadah, from al-Hasan, that the name of this ant was Haras, that she was from a tribe called the Banu al-Shaysan, and that she was lame, and was the size of a wolf.

That is: she feared that the horses would trample the ants with their hooves, so she commanded them to enter their dwellings, and Solomon, upon him be peace, understood this from her.

﴿So he smiled, laughing at her word, and said, "My Lord, enable me to be grateful for Your favor which You have bestowed upon me and upon my parents, and to do righteousness that pleases You."﴾ That is: inspire me to thank You for Your blessing which You have bestowed upon me, by teaching me the speech of birds and animals, and upon my parents by Islam to You and faith in You; ﴿"and to do righteousness that pleases You"﴾, that is, deeds that You love and are pleased with; ﴿"And admit me by Your mercy among Your righteous servants"﴾, that is: when You take my soul, join me to the righteous among Your servants and to the highest companionship among Your friends.

As for those among the commentators who said that this valley was in the land of al-Sham or elsewhere, and that this ant had two wings like a fly, or other such sayings, there is no benefit in them.

It was related from Nawf al-Bakali that he said: "The ants of Solomon were like wolves." I have seen it vocalized with a dot beneath the letter (ياء مثناة من تحت, the letter *ya'* with two dots below) — but it is actually with a dot above the letter (باء موحدة, the letter *ba'* with one dot below). That is an error in copying, and God knows best.

The point is that Solomon, upon him be peace, understood her words and smiled, laughing at that, and this is a very great matter.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father related to us, Muhammad ibn Bashshar related to us, Yazid ibn Harun related to us, Mis'ar informed us, from Zayd al-'Ammi, from Abu al-Siddiq al-Naji, who said: Solomon, upon him be peace, went out seeking rain, and he came upon an ant lying on its back, raising its legs toward the sky, and it was saying: "O God, we are a creation from Your creation, and we have no independence from Your watering; if You do not water us, You will destroy us." Solomon, upon him be peace, said: "Return, for you have been watered by the supplication of others than you."

It is established in the Sahih (in Muslim) by way of 'Abd al-Razzaq, from Ma'mar, from Hammam, from Abu Hurayrah, from the Prophet (ﷺ) [who said]: "A prophet among the prophets was bitten by an ant, so he ordered the ants' settlement to be burned. God revealed to him: 'Because an ant bit you, you destroyed a nation of the nations that glorify God? Would that it had been one ant!'" [Sahih Muslim, no. 2241.]

Then Solomon, upon him be peace, said to the birds: 'Shade David!' So the birds shaded him until the earth was darkened over them both. Then Solomon said to them: 'Fold your wings one by one.'" Abu Hurayrah said: "O Messenger of God, how did the birds do it?" So the Messenger of God (ﷺ) closed his hand, and on that day the *mudrahiyyah* overcame him. [Al-Musnad (2/419). Al-Haythami said in al-Majma' (8/206): "In it is al-Muttalib ibn 'Abd Allah ibn Hanatab, whom Abu Zur'ah and others declared trustworthy, and the rest of its narrators are narrators of the Sahih."]

Abu al-Faraj ibn al-Jawzi said: *al-Mudrahiyyah* (المضرحية) [in the manuscripts: "al-Mus.rahiyyah," and the version adopted from Lisan al-'Arab, entry "d-r-h"] means the red vultures.

* *

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And there were gathered for Solomon his hosts of jinn and men and birds, and they were marshaled in ranks﴾ means: his hosts were assembled for Solomon from the jinn, the men, and the birds, meaning that he rode among them in great pomp and majesty. Among mankind were those closest to him, the jinn came next in rank, and the birds had their station above his head, so that if the sun was hot, they shaded him with their wings.

* *

His saying: ﴿So they were marshaled in ranks﴾ means: the first of them was held back to the last of them, so that no one would advance beyond his proper station, which was assigned to him.

Mujahid said: He appointed over each kind guards who turned back its first members to its last, so that they would not advance ahead during the march, as kings do today.

* *

His saying: ﴿Until, when they came upon the valley of the ants﴾ means: until, when Solomon, upon him be peace, passed with those of the armies and hosts who were with him, upon the valley of the ants, ﴿a female ant said, "O ants, enter your dwellings, lest Solomon and his hosts crush you while they do not perceive."﴾

Ibn 'Asakir related, by way of Ishaq ibn Bishr, from Sa'id, from Qatadah, from al-Hasan, that the name of this ant was Haras, that she was from a tribe called the Banu al-Shaysan, and that she was lame, and was the size of a wolf.

That is: she feared that the horses would trample the ants with their hooves, so she commanded them to enter their dwellings, and Solomon, upon him be peace, understood this from her.

﴿So he smiled, laughing at her word, and said, "My Lord, enable me to be grateful for Your favor which You have bestowed upon me and upon my parents, and to do righteousness that pleases You."﴾ That is: inspire me to thank You for Your blessing which You have bestowed upon me, by teaching me the speech of birds and animals, and upon my parents by Islam to You and faith in You; ﴿"and to do righteousness that pleases You"﴾, that is, deeds that You love and are pleased with; ﴿"And admit me by Your mercy among Your righteous servants"﴾, that is: when You take my soul, join me to the righteous among Your servants and to the highest companionship among Your friends.

As for those among the commentators who said that this valley was in the land of al-Sham or elsewhere, and that this ant had two wings like a fly, or other such sayings, there is no benefit in them.

It was related from Nawf al-Bakali that he said: "The ants of Solomon were like wolves." I have seen it vocalized with a dot beneath the letter (ياء مثناة من تحت, the letter *ya'* with two dots below) — but it is actually with a dot above the letter (باء موحدة, the letter *ba'* with one dot below). That is an error in copying, and God knows best.

The point is that Solomon, upon him be peace, understood her words and smiled, laughing at that, and this is a very great matter.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father related to us, Muhammad ibn Bashshar related to us, Yazid ibn Harun related to us, Mis'ar informed us, from Zayd al-'Ammi, from Abu al-Siddiq al-Naji, who said: Solomon, upon him be peace, went out seeking rain, and he came upon an ant lying on its back, raising its legs toward the sky, and it was saying: "O God, we are a creation from Your creation, and we have no independence from Your watering; if You do not water us, You will destroy us." Solomon, upon him be peace, said: "Return, for you have been watered by the supplication of others than you."

It is established in the Sahih (in Muslim) by way of 'Abd al-Razzaq, from Ma'mar, from Hammam, from Abu Hurayrah, from the Prophet (ﷺ) [who said]: "A prophet among the prophets was bitten by an ant, so he ordered the ants' settlement to be burned. God revealed to him: 'Because an ant bit you, you destroyed a nation of the nations that glorify God? Would that it had been one ant!'" [Sahih Muslim, no. 2241.]

Mujahid, Sa'id ibn Jubayr and others, on the authority of Ibn Abbas and others, said: The hoopoe was an engineer (muhandis) who guided Sulayman, peace be upon him, to water. When he was in a barren desert, he would search for water and see it beneath the surface of the earth, just as a person sees a visible object on the face of the earth. He would also know how far away it was from the surface. When he showed them where it was, Sulayman, peace be upon him, ordered the jinn, and they dug at that spot until the water was extracted from its depths. Once, Sulayman, peace be upon him, stopped in a desert place and inspected the birds to see the hoopoe, but he did not see it. ﴿He said, "Why is it that I do not see the hoopoe? Or is it among the absent?"﴾

Ibn Abbas once related something similar to this, and among the people was a man from the Khawarij (a dissenting sect), called Nafi' ibn al-Azraq, who often objected to Ibn Abbas. He said to him: "Stop, O Ibn Abbas! You have been defeated today!" He said: "Why?" He said: "You claim that the hoopoe sees water beneath the surface of the earth, yet a boy places a grain in a trap, covers the trap with dirt, and the hoopoe comes to take the grain, falls into the trap, and the boy catches it." Ibn Abbas said: "Were it not that this would lead someone to say, 'You refuted Ibn Abbas,' I would not answer you." Then he said to him: "Woe to you! When the decree descends, sight becomes blind and caution departs." Nafi' said to him: "By God, I will never dispute with you about anything from the Qur'an, ever." [Narrated by al-Hakim in al-Mustadrak (2/405) through al-Minhal ibn Amr, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, in similar wording.]

Ibn Asakir mentioned, in the biography of Abu Abdullah al-Barzi, a man of Barzah in the Ghouta of Damascus, who was among the righteous, fasted on Mondays and Thursdays, and was one-eyed, having reached eighty years of age, that Ibn Asakir related with his chain to Abu Sulayman ibn Zayd that he asked him about the cause of his blindness. He refused to tell him, so he insisted for months, and then he informed him that two men from Khurasan stayed with him for a week in the village of Barzah and asked him about a valley there. He showed them it, and they brought out censers and lit a great deal of incense in them, until the valley was filled with smoke. They began to invoke spells while snakes came toward them from every direction, but they paid no attention to any of them, until a snake approached them, about the length of a forearm, its eyes blazing like dinars. They rejoiced greatly at it and said, "Praise be to God who did not disappoint our journey from a year ago." They broke the censers, took the snake, and put a metal rod (mil) into its eye and applied it as kohl. I asked them to apply it to my eyes, but they refused. I insisted on them and said, "This must be done," and threatened them with the authorities, so they applied it to my right eye. When it entered my eye, I looked at the ground beneath me as if it were a mirror, seeing what was beneath it as a mirror reflects. Then they said to me, "Walk with us a little." I walked with them while they talked, until, when I had moved away from the village, they seized me, bound me, and one of them put his hand into my eye and gouged it out, threw it away, and they departed. I remained there, bound and cast down, until a group passed by me and untied my bonds. This is the account of my eye.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Ali ibn al-Husayn related to us, Hisham ibn Ammar related to us, Sadaqah ibn Amr al-Ghassani related to us, Abbad ibn Maysara al-Minqari related to us, from al-Hasan, who said: The name of Sulayman's hoopoe, peace be upon him, was Anbar.

Muhammad ibn Ishaq said: When Sulayman, peace be upon him, went out in the morning to his assembly where he used to sit, he inspected the birds. It was said that each day a group of every kind of bird would come to him, one bird each day. He looked and saw all kinds of birds present except the hoopoe. ﴿He said, "Why is it that I do not see the hoopoe? Or is it among the absent?"﴾ "My sight missed it among the birds, or it was absent and did not attend?"

* *

As for His words, ﴿I will surely punish him with a severe punishment﴾: al-A'mash related from al-Minhal ibn Amr, from Sa'id, from Ibn Abbas: this means plucking out its feathers.

Abdullah ibn Shaddad said: plucking out its feathers and exposing it to the sun. Likewise more than one of the early scholars said: it means plucking out its feathers and leaving it cast aside, to be eaten by ants and insects.

* *

As for His words, ﴿or I will surely slaughter him﴾: meaning, kill him. ﴿Or he must bring me a clear authority﴾: that is, a manifest and clear excuse.

Sufyan ibn Uyaynah and Abdullah ibn Shaddad said: When the hoopoe came, the birds said to him: "What kept you back? Sulayman has vowed to shed your blood!" He said: "Did he make an exception?" They said: "Yes." He said: ﴿"I will surely punish him with a severe punishment, or I will surely slaughter him, or he must bring me a clear authority."﴾ So he said: "Then I have escaped."

Mujahid said: God only repelled [the punishment] from him because of his kindness to his mother.

Ibn Kathir said, may Allah the Exalted have mercy on him: ﴿He stayed﴾ the hoopoe ﴿not long﴾, meaning he was absent for a short time. Then he came and said to Sulayman: ﴿I have comprehended what you have not comprehended﴾, meaning I have learned what neither you nor your soldiers have learned, ﴿and I have come to you from Saba' with certain news﴾, meaning with true, certain news.

Saba' (Sheba) are the Himyar, who were the kings of Yemen.

Then he said: ﴿I found a woman ruling over them﴾. Al-Hasan al-Basri said: She is Bilqis, daughter of Sharahil, the queen of Saba'.

Qatadah said: Her mother was a jinn, and the back of her feet was like the hoof of a beast. She was from a royal house.

Zuhayr ibn Muhammad said: She is Bilqis, daughter of Sharahil ibn Malik ibn al-Rayyan, and her mother was Fari'ah the jinn.

Ibn Juraij said: Bilqis, daughter of Dhu Sharkh, and her mother was Yaltaqah.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: 'Ali ibn al-Husayn related to us, Musaddad related to us, Sufyan (meaning Ibn 'Uyaynah) related to us, from 'Ata' ibn al-Sa'ib, from Mujahid, from Ibn 'Abbas who said: With the companion [in f: "the companion of"] of Sulayman there were a thousand qayls (chieftains), under each qayl were one hundred thousand [fighting men] [[Addition from f and a.]].

Al-A'mash said, from Mujahid: Under the authority of the queen of Saba' were twelve thousand qayls, under each qayl one hundred thousand fighting men.

'Abd al-Razzaq said: Ma'mar informed us, from Qatadah, regarding His saying ﴿I found a woman ruling over them﴾: She was from a royal house, and her chief counsellors were three hundred and twelve men, each of whom was over ten thousand men. She was in a land called Ma'rib, three miles from San'a'.

This view is the closest to the truth, in that it [the kingdom] was extensive relative to the kingdom of Yemen. And Allah knows best.

* *

His saying: ﴿And she has been given of everything﴾, meaning of the goods of this world what a powerful king needs. ﴿And she has a great throne﴾.

That is, a seat on which she sits, great and imposing, adorned with gold and various kinds of jewels and pearls.

Zuhayr ibn Muhammad said: It was of gold, its two sides inlaid with rubies and chrysolite [[the text here continues: its length was eighty cubits and its width forty cubits.]] and, Muhammad ibn Ishaq said: it was of gold, set with rubies, chrysolite and pearls. Only women served her, and six hundred women were in charge of the service [in f: "a woman in charge of her"].

The historians said: This throne was in a great, lofty, well-built palace, with three hundred and sixty windows on its eastern side and the same number on its western side, its construction arranged so that the sun would enter through one window each day and set through the window opposite it, so they would prostrate to it in the morning and evening. For this reason He said: ﴿I found her and her people prostrating to the sun instead of Allah, and Satan has made their deeds appear fair to them and averted them from the way﴾, meaning from the path of truth, ﴿so they are not guided﴾.

* *

His saying: ﴿Not to prostrate to Allah﴾ [its meaning: ﴿and Satan has made their deeds appear fair to them and averted them from the way, so they are not guided, not to prostrate to Allah﴾] [[Addition from f and a.]], meaning they do not know the path of truth, which is to devote prostration to Allah alone, rather than to anything He created among the stars or other things, as He the Exalted said: ﴿And among His signs are the night and the day, and the sun and the moon. Do not prostrate to the sun or the moon, but prostrate to Allah who created them, if it is Him that you worship﴾ [Fussilat: 37].

Some readers recited: "Alā yā isjudū lillāh" [أَلَا يَا اسْجُدُوا لِلَّهِ]. They took "alā" as the introductory particle, and "yā" as the vocative particle, and the object of address was omitted; its implied form is: "Alā yā qawmi, isjudū lillāh" ("Ah, O my people, prostrate to Allah").

* *

His saying: ﴿He who brings forth the hidden [khabʾ] in the heavens and the earth﴾. 'Ali ibn Abi Talhah related from Ibn 'Abbas: He knows every hidden thing in the heaven and the earth. Likewise said 'Ikrimah, Mujahid, Sa'id ibn Jubayr, Qatadah, and others.

Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab said: al-khabʾ is the water. Likewise said 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd ibn Aslam: The hidden things of the heavens and the earth are what has been placed in them of provisions: the rain from the sky and the plants from the earth.

This is appropriate in the speech of the hoopoe, to whom Allah gave the special quality that Ibn 'Abbas and others mentioned, namely that he sees water flowing in the depths and inner parts of the earth.

* *

His saying: ﴿And He knows what you conceal and what you reveal﴾, meaning He knows what the servants hide and what they make public of words and deeds. This is like His saying the Exalted: ﴿It is the same whether one of you conceals speech or speaks it openly, and whether he hides by night or goes forth freely by day﴾ [al-Ra'd: 10].

* *

(3223), with the wording: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) forbade killing the surad, the frog, the ant and the hoopoe." Commentary of Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Qur'an al-'Azim) on Surah 27, verses 32–35:

When she read to them the letter of Sulayman, she consulted them about her matter and about what had befallen her. For this reason she said: ﴿O chiefs, advise me in my affair. I would not decide any matter until you are present with me.﴾ That is, until you attend and give your counsel.

﴿They said: "We are possessed of strength and possessed of great might."﴾ That is, they boasted to her of their numbers, their multitude and their power. Then they left the matter to her, saying: ﴿"But the command is yours, so consider what you will command."﴾ That is, we have no hindrance, and we have no might [in opposition to him]. If you wish to confront him and fight him, we have no obstacle to that. After all this, the command is yours. Command us according to your opinion, and we will comply with it and obey it.

Al-Hasan al-Basri, may Allah have mercy on him, said: They entrusted their affair to a rough woman whose breasts were shaking. When they had said to her what they said, she was more resolute in judgment than they were and more knowledgeable about the affair of Sulayman. She knew that she had no power against his soldiers and his armies, or against what had been subjected to him of jinn, humans and birds. She had also witnessed, in the matter of the letter with the hoopoe, a wondrous and marvellous affair. So she said to them: "I fear that if we fight him and resist him, he will march against us with his soldiers, destroy us along with those who are with us, and ruin and annihilation will reach me and you, while others remain unharmed." For this reason she said: ﴿"Indeed, when kings enter a town, they corrupt it"﴾.

Ibn 'Abbas said: That is, when they enter a land by force, they corrupt it, meaning they ruin it. ﴿"And they make the most honourable of its people the most humiliated"﴾. That is, they target those in it among the governors and soldiers, and they humiliate them to the utmost degree of humiliation, either by killing them or by taking them captive.

Ibn 'Abbas said: Bilqis said: ﴿"Indeed, when kings enter a town, they corrupt it and make the most honourable of its people the most humiliated."﴾ Then the Lord, Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿"And thus they do."﴾ Then she turned to conciliation, reconciliation, peace-making, deception and flattery, and said: ﴿"Indeed, I am going to send them a gift and see with what the envoys will return."﴾ That is: I will send to him a gift befitting him, and I will see what his response will be after that. Perhaps he will accept it and refrain from us, or he will impose upon us a tribute which we will bring to him every year, and we will commit ourselves to that, and he will abandon fighting and warring against us. Qatadah said: May Allah have mercy on her and be pleased with her! How intelligent she was, both in her Islam and in her polytheism! She knew that a gift has an effect on people.

Ibn 'Abbas and others said: She said to her people: If he accepts the gift, then he is a king, so fight him; and if he does not accept it, then he is a prophet, so follow him.

Mujahid, Sa'id ibn Jubayr and others said: She sent young women dressed as boys and boys dressed as young women, and said: "If he can tell these from those, then he is a prophet." They said: So Sulayman, peace be upon him, ordered them to perform ablution. The young woman began pouring water over her hand, while the boy began scooping it up, and he distinguished them by this.

It was also said: Rather, the young woman began washing the inside of her hand before the outside, and the boy did the reverse.

It was also said: Rather, the young women washed from their palms up to their elbows, and the boys from their elbows down to their palms. There is no contradiction among all of these, and Allah knows best.

Some of them mentioned that she sent him a cup to fill with fresh water, neither from the sky nor from the earth. So he made the horses run until they sweated, then filled the cup with that sweat. She also sent a bored pearl with a thread, so that he would put the thread through it, and he did so. Allah knows whether this happened or not, and most of it is taken from the Isra'iliyyat (narrations of Israelite origin). The apparent meaning is that Sulayman, peace be upon him, did not look at what they had brought at all, nor did he give it any attention; rather he turned away from it, and said, denouncing them: ﴿Do you provide me with wealth?﴾ That is, do you try to win me over with wealth so that I will leave you to your polytheism and your kingdom? ﴿What Allah has given me is better than what He has given you﴾ That is, what Allah has given me of kingship, wealth and armies is better than what you have. ﴿Rather, you rejoice in your gift﴾ That is, you are the ones who yield to gifts and presents, whereas I accept from you nothing but Islam or the sword.

In this there is evidence for the permissibility of kings adorning themselves and displaying their finery before envoys and delegations.

She sent to him: "I am coming to you with the nobles of my people, so that I may see what your command is and what you call us to of your religion." Then she ordered the throne of her kingdom, on which she used to sit, to be brought out. It was of gold, inlaid with rubies, emeralds and pearls. It was placed in seven chambers, one inside another, and then she locked the doors upon it. Then she said to whoever she had left in charge of her realm: "Guard what is in your charge, and the throne of my kingdom. Let none of Allah's servants reach it, and let no one see it until I come to you." Then she set out to Sulayman with twelve thousand qayls (chieftains) of the kings of Yemen, under each of whom were many thousands. Sulayman began sending the jinn to bring him news of her march and her destination every day and night. When she drew near, he gathered those around him of the jinn and mankind who were under his command, and said: ﴿O chiefs, which of you will bring me her throne before they come to me in submission?﴾

Qatadah said: When it reached Sulayman that she was coming, he had been told about her throne and it had pleased him. It was made of gold, its legs were of pearl and jewels, it was covered with brocade and silk, and it had nine locks upon it. He disliked to take it after they had become Muslims. The Prophet of Allah knew that once they embraced Islam, their wealth would become forbidden to be taken, along with their blood. Commentary of Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Quran al-'Azim) on surah 27, verses 41–44 (part 1 of 2):

When Sulayman (peace be upon him) was brought the throne of Bilqis before her arrival, he ordered that some of its attributes be altered, in order to test her recognition of it and her steadfastness when she saw it, whether she would affirm that it was her throne or that it was not. He said: ﴿Disguise her throne for her; we will see whether she is guided or is among those who are not guided.﴾

Ibn 'Abbas said: he removed its inlays (fusus) and its joints (marafiq).

Mujahid said: he ordered it changed, so that what was red was made yellow, what was yellow was made red, and what was green was made red. Everything was altered from its state.

Ikrimah said: they added to it and subtracted from it.

[Qatadah said: they made its lower part its upper part and its front its back, and they added to it and subtracted from it.] [[Addition from manuscripts F and A.]]

﴿So when she came, it was said: "Is your throne like this?"﴾ That is, her throne was presented to her after it had been altered, disguised, added to and subtracted from. She had steadfastness and intellect, and she had wisdom, shrewdness and prudence. So she did not affirm that it was it, because of the great distance it had come, nor did she deny that it was it, because of the signs and attributes she recognised in it, even though it had been altered, changed and disguised. So she said: ﴿It is as if it were it﴾, that is, it resembles it and is close to it. This is the utmost in intelligence and prudence.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿And we were given the knowledge before her, and we were Muslims﴾, Mujahid said: it is Sulayman who says this.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿And what she used to worship besides Allah had barred her; indeed she was from a disbelieving people﴾, this is part of Sulayman's speech (peace be upon him), according to the view of Mujahid and Sa'id ibn Jubayr, may Allah have mercy on them both. That is, Sulayman said: ﴿And we were given the knowledge before her, and we were Muslims﴾, and [she] had been barred, meaning prevented from worshipping Allah alone. ﴿What she used to worship besides Allah; indeed she was from a disbelieving people.﴾ This is what Mujahid and Sa'id said, and it is good. Ibn Jarir (al-Tabari) also said it.

Then Ibn Jarir said: It is also possible that the pronoun in ﴿And had barred her﴾ refers back to Sulayman or to Allah, Mighty and Majestic, the sense being: and [He/he] prevented her ﴿from what she used to worship besides Allah﴾, that is, He barred her from worshipping other than Allah. ﴿Indeed she was from a disbelieving people.﴾

I say: What supports the view of Mujahid is that she only displayed Islam after entering the palace (sarh), as will come.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿It was said to her: "Enter the palace." And when she saw it, she thought it was a pool, and she uncovered her shins﴾: Sulayman (peace be upon him) commanded the devils, and they built for her a great palace of qawarir, that is, of glass, and he made water flow beneath it. Whoever did not know its matter would think it was water, but the glass lies between the walker and the water. The scholars differed concerning the reason that prompted Sulayman (peace be upon him) to make it. It is said that when he resolved to marry her and take her for himself, he was told of her beauty and loveliness, but there was thick hair on her shins, and the back of her feet was like the hind part of an animal. This displeased him, so he made this (the palace) to learn whether it was true or not. This is the view of Muhammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazi and others. When she entered and uncovered her shins, he saw that she was the most beautiful of people and the finest of feet, but he saw hair on her legs, because she was a queen who had no husband, so he wished that this would be removed from her. It was said to her: "Is it the razor?" She said: "I cannot do that." Sulayman disliked this and said to the jinn: "Make something other than the razor that will remove this hair," and they made for him depilatory cream (nurah). He was the first for whom depilatory cream was made. This was said by Ibn 'Abbas, Mujahid, Ikrimah, Muhammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazi, al-Suddi, Ibn Jurayj and others.

Muhammad ibn Ishaq said, from Yazid ibn Ruman: Then he said to her: "Enter the palace," so that he might show her a kingdom more honourable than her kingdom and an authority greater than her authority. ﴿When she saw it, she thought it was a pool, and she uncovered her shins﴾, not doubting that it was water she was wading through. It was said to her: it is a palace paved with glass (mumarrad min qawarir). When she stood before Sulayman, he invited her to worship Allah and rebuked her for worshipping the sun besides Allah.

Al-Hasan al-Basri said: When the woman (al-'ilja) saw the palace, she knew, by Allah, that she had seen a kingdom greater than her kingdom.

Muhammad ibn Ishaq said, from a man of knowledge, from Wahb ibn Munabbih, who said: Sulayman ordered the palace, which the devils had made for him of glass, appearing like water in its whiteness. Then he let water flow beneath it, and his throne was placed in it, and he sat upon it, and the birds, jinn and humans gathered around him. Then he said: "Enter the palace," so that he might show her a kingdom more honourable than her kingdom and an authority greater than her authority. ﴿When she saw it, she thought it was a pool, and she uncovered her shins﴾, not doubting that it was water she was wading through. It was said to her: ﴿It is a palace paved with glass﴾. When she stood before Sulayman, he invited her to worship Allah, Mighty and Majestic, and rebuked her for worshipping the sun besides Allah. She then spoke with the words of the zanadiqa (heretics), so Sulayman fell down in prostration out of reverence for what she had said, and the people prostrated with him. Her heart sank when she saw Sulayman do what he did. When Sulayman raised his head he said: "Woe to you! What did you say?" She forgot what she had said, and she said: ﴿My Lord, I have wronged myself, and I have submitted with Sulayman to Allah, Lord of the worlds.﴾ So she became Muslim and her Islam was good.

Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah has related in this a strange report (athar gharib) from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: al-Husayn ibn 'Ali told us, from Za'idah, who said: 'Ata ibn al-Sa'ib told me, from Mujahid, who said, while we were among the Azd: Ibn 'Abbas told us that Sulayman (peace be upon him) used to sit upon his throne, then chairs were placed around him, and the humans sat on them, then the jinn sat, then the devils. Then the wind came and lifted them, then the birds shaded them. Then they travelled in the morning a distance that a rider would wish to rest after a month, and in the evening likewise a month's journey. He said: One day, while he was on a journey, he inspected the birds and missed the hoopoe, and he said: ﴿Why do I not see the hoopoe? Or is he among the absent? I will surely punish him with a severe punishment, or I will surely slaughter him, or he must bring me a clear authority.﴾ He said: His punishment of it was to pluck its feathers and then throw it on the ground, so that it could not escape from an ant or any creeping thing of the earth.

'Ata said: Sa'id ibn Jubayr mentioned from Ibn 'Abbas the same as the hadith of Mujahid. ﴿But he stayed not long﴾, then he recited until he reached His saying ﴿He said: "We shall see whether you have told the truth or were among the liars. Go with this letter of mine and deliver it"﴾, and he wrote: ﴿In the name of Allah, the Most Merciful, the Especially Merciful﴾, to Bilqis: ﴿Do not exalt yourselves over me, and come to me in submission.﴾ When the hoopoe threw the letter to her, it was cast into her heart that it was a noble letter, that it was from Sulayman, and that she should not exalt herself over him and should come to him in submission. They said: "We are people of strength." She said: "Indeed, when kings enter a town they corrupt it, and I will send to them a gift." When the gift came to Sulayman, he said: "Do you provide me with wealth? Return to them." When he looked at the dust (of the approaching army)—Ibn 'Abbas told us: the distance between Sulayman and the queen of Saba' and those with her, when he looked at the dust, was like the distance between us and al-Hirah; 'Ata said, and Mujahid was then among the Azd—Sulayman said: "Which of you will bring me her throne?" He said: the distance between her throne and Sulayman, when he looked at the dust, was two months' journey. ﴿An 'ifrit of the jinn said: "I will bring it to you before you rise from your place."﴾ He said: Sulayman had an assembly in which he sat with the people, as rulers sit, and then he would rise. He said: ﴿I will bring it to you before you rise from your place.﴾ Sulayman said: "I want it more quickly than that." Ibn 'Abbas said: he removed its inlays (fusus) and its joints (marafiq).

* *

He said: Sulayman leapt from his couch and fell down in prostration, and said: "O Lord, she has asked me about a matter that is too great for my heart to mention to You." He said: "Return, for I have sufficed you against them." He said: So he returned to his couch and said: "What did you ask about?" She said: "I asked you only about the water." He said to his soldiers: "What did she ask about?" They said: "She asked you only about the water." He said: They all forgot it. He said: The devils said to Sulayman: "Do you want to take her for yourself? If he takes her for himself and a child is born between them, we will never be freed from his servitude." He said: So they made a palace paved with glass, in which there were fish. He said: It was said to her: ﴿Enter the palace.﴾ ﴿When she saw it, she thought it was a pool, and she uncovered her shins﴾, and behold, they were hairy. Then Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah said: How good this hadith is.

Commentary of Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Quran al-'Azim) on surah 27, verses 41–44 (part 1 of 2):

When Sulayman (peace be upon him) was brought the throne of Bilqis before her arrival, he ordered that some of its attributes be altered, in order to test her recognition of it and her steadfastness when she saw it, whether she would affirm that it was her throne or that it was not. He said: ﴿Disguise her throne for her; we will see whether she is guided or is among those who are not guided.﴾

Ibn 'Abbas said: he removed its inlays (fusus) and its joints (marafiq).

Mujahid said: he ordered it changed, so that what was red was made yellow, what was yellow was made red, and what was green was made red. Everything was altered from its state.

Ikrimah said: they added to it and subtracted from it.

[Qatadah said: they made its lower part its upper part and its front its back, and they added to it and subtracted from it.] [[Addition from manuscripts F and A.]]

﴿So when she came, it was said: "Is your throne like this?"﴾ That is, her throne was presented to her after it had been altered, disguised, added to and subtracted from. She had steadfastness and intellect, and she had wisdom, shrewdness and prudence. So she did not affirm that it was it, because of the great distance it had come, nor did she deny that it was it, because of the signs and attributes she recognised in it, even though it had been altered, changed and disguised. So she said: ﴿It is as if it were it﴾, that is, it resembles it and is close to it. This is the utmost in intelligence and prudence.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿And we were given the knowledge before her, and we were Muslims﴾, Mujahid said: it is Sulayman who says this.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿And what she used to worship besides Allah had barred her; indeed she was from a disbelieving people﴾, this is part of Sulayman's speech (peace be upon him), according to the view of Mujahid and Sa'id ibn Jubayr, may Allah have mercy on them both. That is, Sulayman said: ﴿And we were given the knowledge before her, and we were Muslims﴾, and [she] had been barred, meaning prevented from worshipping Allah alone. ﴿What she used to worship besides Allah; indeed she was from a disbelieving people.﴾ This is what Mujahid and Sa'id said, and it is good. Ibn Jarir (al-Tabari) also said it.

Then Ibn Jarir said: It is also possible that the pronoun in ﴿And had barred her﴾ refers back to Sulayman or to Allah, Mighty and Majestic, the sense being: and [He/he] prevented her ﴿from what she used to worship besides Allah﴾, that is, He barred her from worshipping other than Allah. ﴿Indeed she was from a disbelieving people.﴾

I say: What supports the view of Mujahid is that she only displayed Islam after entering the palace (sarh), as will come.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿It was said to her: "Enter the palace." And when she saw it, she thought it was a pool, and she uncovered her shins﴾: Sulayman (peace be upon him) commanded the devils, and they built for her a great palace of qawarir, that is, of glass, and he made water flow beneath it. Whoever did not know its matter would think it was water, but the glass lies between the walker and the water. The scholars differed concerning the reason that prompted Sulayman (peace be upon him) to make it. It is said that when he resolved to marry her and take her for himself, he was told of her beauty and loveliness, but there was thick hair on her shins, and the back of her feet was like the hind part of an animal. This displeased him, so he made this (the palace) to learn whether it was true or not. This is the view of Muhammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazi and others. When she entered and uncovered her shins, he saw that she was the most beautiful of people and the finest of feet, but he saw hair on her legs, because she was a queen who had no husband, so he wished that this would be removed from her. It was said to her: "Is it the razor?" She said: "I cannot do that." Sulayman disliked this and said to the jinn: "Make something other than the razor that will remove this hair," and they made for him depilatory cream (nurah). He was the first for whom depilatory cream was made. This was said by Ibn 'Abbas, Mujahid, Ikrimah, Muhammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazi, al-Suddi, Ibn Jurayj and others.

Muhammad ibn Ishaq said, from Yazid ibn Ruman: Then he said to her: "Enter the palace," so that he might show her a kingdom more honourable than her kingdom and an authority greater than her authority. ﴿When she saw it, she thought it was a pool, and she uncovered her shins﴾, not doubting that it was water she was wading through. It was said to her: it is a palace paved with glass (mumarrad min qawarir). When she stood before Sulayman, he invited her to worship Allah and rebuked her for worshipping the sun besides Allah.

Al-Hasan al-Basri said: When the woman (al-'ilja) saw the palace, she knew, by Allah, that she had seen a kingdom greater than her kingdom.

Muhammad ibn Ishaq said, from a man of knowledge, from Wahb ibn Munabbih, who said: Sulayman ordered the palace, which the devils had made for him of glass, appearing like water in its whiteness. Then he let water flow beneath it, and his throne was placed in it, and he sat upon it, and the birds, jinn and humans gathered around him. Then he said: "Enter the palace," so that he might show her a kingdom more honourable than her kingdom and an authority greater than her authority. ﴿When she saw it, she thought it was a pool, and she uncovered her shins﴾, not doubting that it was water she was wading through. It was said to her: ﴿It is a palace paved with glass﴾. When she stood before Sulayman, he invited her to worship Allah, Mighty and Majestic, and rebuked her for worshipping the sun besides Allah. She then spoke with the words of the zanadiqa (heretics), so Sulayman fell down in prostration out of reverence for what she had said, and the people prostrated with him. Her heart sank when she saw Sulayman do what he did. When Sulayman raised his head he said: "Woe to you! What did you say?" She forgot what she had said, and she said: ﴿My Lord, I have wronged myself, and I have submitted with Sulayman to Allah, Lord of the worlds.﴾ So she became Muslim and her Islam was good.

Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah has related in this a strange report (athar gharib) from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: al-Husayn ibn 'Ali told us, from Za'idah, who said: 'Ata ibn al-Sa'ib told me, from Mujahid, who said, while we were among the Azd: Ibn 'Abbas told us that Sulayman (peace be upon him) used to sit upon his throne, then chairs were placed around him, and the humans sat on them, then the jinn sat, then the devils. Then the wind came and lifted them, then the birds shaded them. Then they travelled in the morning a distance that a rider would wish to rest after a month, and in the evening likewise a month's journey. He said: One day, while he was on a journey, he inspected the birds and missed the hoopoe, and he said: ﴿Why do I not see the hoopoe? Or is he among the absent? I will surely punish him with a severe punishment, or I will surely slaughter him, or he must bring me a clear authority.﴾ He said: His punishment of it was to pluck its feathers and then throw it on the ground, so that it could not escape from an ant or any creeping thing of the earth.

'Ata said: Sa'id ibn Jubayr mentioned from Ibn 'Abbas the same as the hadith of Mujahid. ﴿But he stayed not long﴾, then he recited until he reached His saying ﴿He said: "We shall see whether you have told the truth or were among the liars. Go with this letter of mine and deliver it"﴾, and he wrote: ﴿In the name of Allah, the Most Merciful, the Especially Merciful﴾, to Bilqis: ﴿Do not exalt yourselves over me, and come to me in submission.﴾ When the hoopoe threw the letter to her, it was cast into her heart that it was a noble letter, that it was from Sulayman, and that she should not exalt herself over him and should come to him in submission. They said: "We are people of strength." She said: "Indeed, when kings enter a town they corrupt it, and I will send to them a gift." When the gift came to Sulayman, he said: "Do you provide me with wealth? Return to them." When he looked at the dust (of the approaching army)—Ibn 'Abbas told us: the distance between Sulayman and the queen of Saba' and those with her, when he looked at the dust, was like the distance between us and al-Hirah; 'Ata said, and Mujahid was then among the Azd—Sulayman said: "Which of you will bring me her throne?" He said: the distance between her throne and Sulayman, when he looked at the dust, was two months' journey. ﴿An 'ifrit of the jinn said: "I will bring it to you before you rise from your place."﴾ He said: Sulayman had an assembly in which he sat with the people, as rulers sit, and then he would rise. He said: ﴿I will bring it to you before you rise from your place.﴾ Sulayman said: "I want it more quickly than that." Then the one who had knowledge of the Scripture said: "I will look into the Book of my Lord, and then I will bring it to you before your glance returns to you." He said: [Sulayman looked at him, and when he had finished speaking, Sulayman restored his gaze] [[Addition from manuscripts F and A.]], and her throne came up from beneath the feet of Sulayman, from beneath a footstool upon which Sulayman used to place his foot before ascending the couch. He said: When Sulayman saw her throne [settled beside him], he said: ﴿This is of the bounty of my Lord﴾. ﴿He said: "Disguise her throne for her."﴾ When she came, it was said to her: "Is your throne like this?" She said: "It is as if it were it." He said: Then she asked him about two matters. She said to Sulayman: "I want water [of foam, sweet and clear] [[Addition from manuscript F.]] that is neither from the earth nor from the sky." Sulayman, whenever he was asked about something, would ask the humans, then the jinn, then the devils. [He said] [[Addition from manuscript F.]] The devils said: "This is easy. Make the horses run, then take their sweat and fill the vessel with it." He ordered the horses to be made to run, and then he took their sweat and filled the vessel with it. He said: She also asked about the colour of Allah, Mighty and Majestic. He said: Sulayman leapt from his couch and fell down in prostration, and said: "O Lord, she has asked me about a matter that is too great for my heart to mention to You." The Almighty informs us about Thamud and their affair with their Prophet Salih, peace be upon him, when Allah sent him to them. He called them to worship Allah alone, without partner. ﴿Then they became two factions disputing with each other.﴾ Mujahid said: "A believer and a disbeliever." This is like His saying: ﴿The eminent ones among his people who were arrogant said to those who were oppressed, to those among them who believed, "Do you know that Salih is sent from his Lord?" They said, "Indeed, we are believers in that with which he has been sent." Those who were arrogant said, "Indeed, we are, in that which you believe, disbelievers."﴾ [Al-A'raf: 75–76].

﴿He said, "O my people, why do you seek to hasten evil before good?"﴾ That is: why do you ask for the punishment to be brought forward, and not seek mercy from Allah? For this reason He said: ﴿Why do you not seek forgiveness from Allah, that perhaps you may receive mercy?﴾ ﴿They said, "We consider you and those with you to be a bad omen."﴾ That is: we have seen nothing but evil in your face and in the faces of those who follow you. The reason is that, due to their wretchedness, whenever any harm befell any of them, they would say, "This is from Salih and his companions."

Mujahid said: "They considered them a bad omen." This is like His saying, reporting about the people of Pharaoh: ﴿But when good came to them, they said, "This is ours," and if evil afflicted them, they ascribed it to Moses and those with him. Unquestionably, their omen is with Allah.﴾ [Al-A'raf: 131]. He also said: ﴿And if good befalls them, they say, "This is from Allah," and if evil befalls them, they say, "This is from you." Say, "All is from Allah."﴾ [An-Nisa: 78], that is, by the decree of Allah and His predestination. [[In manuscripts F and A: "by the decree of Allah and His predestination."]]

And He said, reporting about the people of the town when the messengers came to it: ﴿They said, "Indeed, we consider you a bad omen. If you do not desist, we will surely stone you, and there will surely touch you from us a painful punishment." They said, "Your omen is with yourselves."﴾ [Ya-Sin: 18–19]. These people said: ﴿"We consider you and those with you a bad omen." He said, "Your omen is with Allah."﴾ That is: Allah will recompense you for that. ﴿Rather, you are a people being tested.﴾ Qatadah said: "You are being tried through obedience and disobedience."

The apparent meaning of His saying ﴿being tested﴾ is: you are being led on gradually (istidraj) in what you are in of misguidance.

The Most High speaks of the tyrants of Thamud and their leaders, who were the ones calling their people to misguidance, disbelief, and denial of Salih. Their situation reached the point that they hamstrung the she-camel, and they also resolved to kill Salih by attacking him at night among his family and slaying him secretly. Then they would say to his close kin: "We knew nothing of his affair," and they would be truthful in what they told them, that they had not witnessed that.

So He, the Most High, said: ﴿And there were in the city﴾, meaning the city of Thamud, ﴿nine men﴾, meaning nine persons, ﴿who spread corruption in the land and did not reform﴾. These were dominant over the affair of Thamud only because they were its great men and its leaders.

Al-'Awfi related from Ibn 'Abbas: "These are the ones who hamstrung the she-camel," meaning that the act proceeded from their opinions and counsel. May Allah disfigure and curse them, for they did it.

Al-Suddi related from Abu Malik, from Ibn 'Abbas: The names of these nine were: Da'ma, Da'im, Hirma, Huraym, Dab, Sawab, Riyab, Mista', and Qudar ibn Salif, the hamstringer of the she-camel, meaning the one who carried out that act with his own hand. Allah the Most High said: ﴿So they called their companion, and he took it in hand and hamstrung it﴾ [al-Qamar: 29], and the Most High said: ﴿When the most wretched of them was sent forth﴾ [al-Shams: 12].

'Abd al-Razzaq said: Yahya ibn Rabi'ah al-San'ani informed us, I heard 'Ata' (that is, Ibn Abi Rabah) say concerning ﴿And there were in the city nine men who spread corruption in the land and did not reform﴾: "They used to clip the dirhams" [Tafsir 'Abd al-Razzaq (2/70)], meaning that they took from them, and it seems they dealt with them by weight as the Arabs used to deal.

Imam Malik said, from Yahya ibn Sa'id, from Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab, that he said: "Cutting gold and silver is among the corruption in the land" [al-Muwatta' (2/635)].

In the hadith narrated by Abu Dawud and others, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) forbade breaking the currency of the Muslims that is in circulation among them, except for a (legitimate) reason [Sunan Abi Dawud, no. 3449].

The point is that these were disbelieving, defiant transgressors, and among their characteristics was corrupting the land by every means they were able to employ. Among these means are those mentioned by these imams and other things.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿They said: "Swear to one another by Allah that we will surely attack him and his family by night"﴾, meaning they made a pact and agreed upon killing the Prophet of Allah Salih (peace be upon him), whoever met him by night, secretly. But Allah outwitted them and turned the calamity back upon them.

Mujahid said: "They pledged and swore to one another to destroy him," but they did not reach him until they were destroyed, together with all their people.

Qatadah said: "They agreed to take him by night and kill him." It was mentioned to us that while they were going toward Salih to ambush him, Allah sent down a rock upon them and crushed them.

Al-'Awfi related from Ibn 'Abbas: "They are the ones who hamstrung the she-camel. When they hamstrung it, they said: 'We will attack Salih and his people by night and kill them, then we will say to the guardians of Salih: We did not witness anything of this, and we have no knowledge of it.'" So Allah destroyed them all.

Muhammad ibn Ishaq said: These nine, after they hamstrung the she-camel, said: "Come, let us kill Salih. If he is truthful, we will hasten him before us; and if he is lying, we will have joined him to his she-camel!" Then he recited: ﴿And they plotted a plot, and We plotted a plot, while they perceived not. So see how was the outcome of their plot: that We destroyed them and their people all together. Those are their houses, desolate, meaning empty, with no one in them, because they wronged. Indeed in that is a sign for a people who know. And We saved those who believed and used to fear Allah﴾.

Ibn Kathir said: Allah, the Exalted, informs about His servant Lut, peace be upon him, that he warned his people of the vengeance of Allah upon them for their committing the abomination which no one among the children of Adam had preceded them in, namely having intercourse with males to the exclusion of females. That is a great abomination: men were satisfied with men and women with women.

He said: ﴿Do you commit the abomination while you see?﴾ That is, some of you see others, and you commit the evil in your gatherings?

﴿Do you really approach men with desire, instead of women? Rather, you are a people who act ignorantly.﴾ That is, you do not recognize anything, neither by natural disposition nor by Sharia. As He said in another verse: ﴿Do you approach the males of the worlds, and leave what your Lord has created for you of your spouses? Rather, you are a people who transgress.﴾ [Ash-Shu'ara': 165, 166].

﴿So the answer of his people was only that they said, "Expel the family of Lut from your town; indeed, they are people who keep themselves pure."﴾ That is, they abstain from what you do and from your approval of your conduct. So expel them from among you, for they are not fit to live as neighbors in your lands. So they resolved upon that, and Allah destroyed them, and the like of it awaits the disbelievers.

Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿So We saved him and his family, except his wife; We had decreed that she be among those who remained behind.﴾ That is, among those who were destroyed along with her people, because she was a supporter of them in their religion and their way, in being pleased with their ugly deeds. She used to direct her people to Lut's guests so that they would go to them. It was not that she committed the abominations herself, out of honor for the Prophet of Allah ﷺ; rather, it was not an honor for her.

The Most High commands His Messenger ﷺ to say: ﴿Praise be to God﴾, meaning for His blessings upon His servants, blessings that cannot be counted or enumerated, and for the sublime attributes and the most beautiful names with which He is described. He also commands him to greet with peace the servants of God whom He chose and selected, who are His messengers and His noble prophets, upon whom be blessings and peace from God. This is what Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd ibn Aslam and others said: that the intended meaning of "His servants whom He chose" is the prophets. He said: this is like His saying: ﴿Glory be to your Lord, the Lord of Might, above what they attribute to Him. And peace be upon the messengers. And praise be to God, Lord of the worlds﴾ [al-Saffat: 180-182].

Al-Thawri and al-Suddi said: they are the Companions of Muhammad ﷺ, may God be pleased with them all. Something similar is narrated from Ibn Abbas.

There is no contradiction. If they are among the servants of God whom He chose, then the prophets are so by a more fitting and more certain right. The purpose is that God, the Most High, commanded His Messenger and those who follow him, after mentioning what He did for His allies of deliverance, victory and support, and what He brought upon His enemies of disgrace, punishment and subjugation, that they should praise Him for all His actions, and that they should greet with peace His chosen and virtuous servants.

Abu Bakr al-Bazzar said: Muhammad ibn Umara ibn Subayh narrated to us; Talq ibn Ghannam narrated to us; al-Hakam ibn Zuhayr narrated to us, from al-Suddi, God willing, from Abu Malik, from Ibn Abbas, regarding ﴿And peace be upon His servants whom He has chosen﴾, that he said: they are the Companions of Muhammad ﷺ, whom God chose for His Prophet, may God be pleased with them.¹

* *

His saying: ﴿Is God better, or what they associate?﴾ is a rhetorical question of rebuke to the polytheists for their worship of other gods alongside God.

Then the Most High began to explain that He alone is the One who creates, provides and governs, to the exclusion of anyone else. So He said: ﴿Who created the heavens and the earth﴾, meaning: those heavens in their loftiness and clarity, and what He placed in them of shining stars, bright planets and revolving orbits; and the earth in its lowness and density, and what He placed in it of mountains, rugged terrain, plains, deserts and wastelands, trees, crops and fruits, seas, animals of various kinds, shapes and colours, and other things.

* *

His saying: ﴿And sent down for you water from the sky﴾, meaning: He made it a provision for the servants. ﴿Then We made to grow thereby gardens﴾, meaning: orchards, ﴿full of beauty﴾, meaning: of fine appearance and lovely form. ﴿It was not for you to make their trees grow﴾, meaning: you were not able to make their trees grow. Only the Creator and Provider can do that, the One who is self-sufficient in that and alone in it, not the idols or rivals that others worship besides Him, as these polytheists themselves acknowledge. As He said in another verse: ﴿If you asked them who created them, they would surely say, "God"﴾ [al-Zukhruf: 87], and ﴿If you asked them who sends down water from the sky and gives life thereby to the earth after its death, they would surely say, "God"﴾ [al-Ankabut: 63]. That is, they acknowledge that He alone is the doer of all of that, with no partner. Yet they worship alongside Him others whom they acknowledge do not create and do not provide. Worship is due only to the One who alone creates and provides. For this reason He said: ﴿Is there a god with God?﴾, meaning: is there a god worshipped along with God? This has been made clear to you, and to every person of understanding it is also clear, from what they themselves acknowledge, that He is the Creator and Provider.

Some commentators say that the meaning of His saying ﴿Is there a god with God?﴾ is: [is there a god with God] who did this? This returns to the same meaning as the first, because the implied answer is that they would say: there is no one who did this with Him; rather He alone did it. Then it is said to them: how then do you worship others with Him, when He is the self-sufficient, sole One who creates and governs? As He said: ﴿Is one who creates like one who does not create?﴾ [al-Nahl: 17].

* *

As for His saying here: ﴿Who created the heavens and the earth﴾: the ﴿Who﴾ (amma) in all these verses is to be understood as: who does these things, like one who has no power over any of them? This is the meaning of the context, even if the other part is not mentioned, because the force of the speech points to it. And He said: ﴿Is God better, or what they associate?﴾.

Then He said at the end of the verse: ﴿Rather, they are a people who ascribe equals﴾, meaning: they make equals and likenesses to God. Likewise, He, the Most High, said: ﴿Is one who is devoutly obedient during the hours of the night, prostrating and standing, fearing the Hereafter and hoping for the mercy of his Lord?﴾ [al-Zumar: 9], meaning: is one who is like this the same as one who is not? For this reason He said: ﴿Say, "Are those who know equal to those who do not know?" Only those of understanding are reminded﴾ [al-Zumar: 9]. And: ﴿So is one whose breast God has opened to Islam, and he is upon light from his Lord, [equal to one who is hard-hearted]? Woe to those whose hearts are hardened against the remembrance of God. Those are in manifest error﴾ [al-Zumar: 22]. And He said: ﴿Is one who stands over every soul in what it has earned [like those who have no such standing]?﴾ [al-Ra'd: 33], meaning: is one who is a witness over the actions of creatures, their movements and their stillness, who knows the unseen, both great and small, the same as those idols they worship, which know nothing, hear nothing and see nothing? For this reason He said: ﴿And they have attributed to God partners. Say, "Name them"﴾ [al-Ra'd: 33]. The same applies to all these noble verses.
