Commentary of Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Quran al-'Azim) on surah 27, verse 61:

He says: ﴿Is He Who made the earth a stable place⦆, i.e., firm, still and fixed, which does not sway or move with its inhabitants nor quake beneath them. For if it were not so, life and living on it would not be pleasant. Rather, out of His grace and mercy, He made it a spread-out expanse (mihad, bisat), firm, not shaking or moving, as He said in the other verse: ﴿It is Allah who made for you the earth a stable place and the sky a structure﴾ [Ghafir: 64].

﴿And placed within it rivers⦆, i.e., He placed in it sweet, good rivers that cut through it within its midst, and He directed them among themselves, from great rivers and small ones and what lies between them, and He sent them east, west, south and north according to the welfare of His servants in their regions and territories, wherever He scattered them across the corners of the earth. He sent to them [[In manuscript A: "to them" (إليهم).]] their provisions according to what they need. ﴿And placed within it firm mountains⦆, i.e., towering mountains that anchor the earth and make it steady, lest it sway with you. ﴿And placed between the two seas a barrier⦆, i.e., He placed between the fresh water and the salt water a barrier (hajiz), meaning a prevention that stops them from mixing, lest this spoil that and that spoil this. For divine wisdom requires that each of them remain in the attribute for which it is intended. The sweet sea is these rivers flowing among the people, and their purpose is that they be sweet, pure and drinkable, giving drink to animals, plants and fruits. The salt seas are those surrounding the regions and territories on every side, and their purpose is that their water be salty and bitter, so that the air is not corrupted by their smell, as Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And it is He who released the two seas, one sweet and palatable and one salty and bitter, and placed between them a barrier and a complete prohibition﴾ [al-Furqan: 53]. Therefore He said: ﴿Is there a god with Allah?⦆, i.e., did He do this? Or is He worshipped after the first statement and the second? Both are sound and mutually implying. ﴿Rather, most of them do not know⦆, i.e., they do not know that they worship other than Him.

Ibn Kathir, in his commentary on Surah an-Naml, verse 62:

He (exalted is He) draws attention to the fact that He is the One who is called upon in times of hardship and the One who is hoped in when calamities befall, as He says: ﴿When harm touches you at sea, those you call upon vanish, except Him﴾ [al-Isra: 67], and He says: ﴿Then when harm touches you, to Him you cry for help﴾ [al-Nahl: 53]. Likewise, He says here: ﴿Who answers the desperate one when he calls upon Him﴾, meaning: who is it to whom the desperate one turns only to Him, and who removes the harm of those in distress other than Him?

Imam Ahmad said: 'Affan narrated to us, Wuhayb narrated to us, Khalid al-Hadhdha' narrated to us, from Abu Tamima al-Hujaymi, from a man from Hujaym, who said: I said, "O Messenger of Allah, to what do you call?" He said: "I call to Allah alone, the One who, if harm touches you and you call upon Him, removes it from you; and the One who, if you are lost in a barren land and you call upon Him, returns you; and the One who, if a year of drought strikes you and you call upon Him, makes things grow for you." He said: I said, "Advise me." He said: "Do not revile anyone, do not disdain any act of kindness, even if it is meeting your brother with a cheerful face, and even if it is pouring from your bucket into the vessel of the one who draws water. Wear your waist-wrap to the middle of the shin, and if you refuse, then to the ankles. Beware of letting the waist-wrap trail, for trailing the waist-wrap is from arrogance, and Allah, blessed and exalted, does not love arrogance." [Addition from F, A, and the Musnad.] [Musnad (5/64).]

Imam Ahmad also narrated it by another route, naming the Companion, saying: 'Affan narrated to us, Hammad ibn Salama narrated to us, Yunus — that is Ibn Ubayd — narrated to us, Ubayda al-Hujaymi narrated to us [in H, F, A: "al-Hujaymi, from his father"], from Abu Tamima al-Hujaymi, from Jabir ibn Sulaym al-Hujaymi, who said: I came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) while he was sitting with his knees drawn up, wrapped in a woollen cloak, the fringe of which had fallen onto his feet. I said: "Which of you is Muhammad — or: the Messenger of Allah?" He gestured with his hand toward himself. I said: "O Messenger of Allah, I am from the desert people, and in me is their harshness, so advise me." He said: "Do not belittle any act of kindness at all, even if it is meeting your brother with a cheerful face, and even if it is pouring from your bucket into the vessel of the one who draws water. If a man reviles you for something he knows about you, do not revile him for something you know about him, for he will have its reward and you will bear its burden. Beware of letting the waist-wrap trail, for trailing the waist-wrap is from arrogance, and Allah does not love arrogance. And do not revile anyone." He said: So I never reviled anyone after that, not a sheep nor a camel. [Musnad (5/63).]

Abu Dawud and al-Nasa'i narrated several routes for this hadith, and in both of them there is a good portion of it. [Sunan Abi Dawud, no. 4084; al-Nasa'i in al-Sunan al-Kubra, nos. 1049–1052.]

Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father narrated to us, Ali ibn Hashim narrated to us [in A: "Hisham"], Abdah ibn Nuh narrated to us, from Umar ibn al-Hajjaj, from Ubayd Allah ibn Abi Salih, who said: Tawus entered upon me to visit me, and I said to him: "Pray to Allah for me, O Abu Abd al-Rahman." He said: "Pray for yourself, for He answers the desperate one when he calls upon Him."

Wahb ibn Munabbih said: I read in the First Book: Allah says, "By My might, whoever seeks refuge in Me, even if the heavens and whoever is in them, and the earth and whoever is on it, plot against him, I will make for him a way out from among them. And whoever does not seek refuge in Me, I will cause the earth to swallow him from beneath his feet, and I will leave him in the air, and I will leave him to himself." [In F: "with whoever"; in A: "that I"; in F: "then He".]

The Hafiz Ibn Asakir mentioned, in the biography of a man from whom Abu Bakr Muhammad ibn Dawud al-Dinawari, known as al-Daqqi al-Sufi, related, that this man said: I used to hire out my mule from Damascus to the town of al-Zabadani. Once a man rode with me, and we passed along a certain road, an unused path, and he said to me: "Take this one, for it is shorter." I said: "I have no knowledge of it." He said: "No, it is shorter." So we took it, and we reached a rugged place and a deep valley, in which there were many slain. He said to me: "Hold the mule's head until I dismount." He dismounted, rolled up his sleeves, gathered his garments around him, drew a knife he had with him, and came at me. I fled from before him, and he pursued me. I adjured him by Allah and said: "Take the mule with what is on it." He said: "It is mine, and I only want to kill you." I warned him of Allah and of punishment, but he would not accept. So I surrendered before him and said: "If you see fit to leave me until I pray two rak'ahs?" He said: "Pray, and be quick." So I stood to pray, and the Qur'an became confused for me, and not a single letter of it came to mind. I remained standing, bewildered, while he said: "Come on! Finish!" Then Allah caused the words of His saying to come to my tongue: ﴿Who answers the desperate one when he calls upon Him, and removes the evil﴾. Suddenly, there was a horseman coming from the mouth of the valley, with a spear in his hand, and he threw it at the man, and it did not miss his heart, so he fell prostrate. I clung to the horseman and said: "By Allah, who are you?" He said: "I am the messenger of the One who answers the desperate one when he calls upon Him, and removes the evil." He said: So I took the mule and its load and returned safely.

It is mentioned in the biography of "Fatima bint al-Hasan, Umm Ahmad al-Ijliyya," that she said: One day the disbelievers defeated the Muslims in a military campaign. A noble, swift horse stopped with its rider, and the rider was one of the wealthy and righteous men. He said to the horse: "What is wrong with you? Woe to you! I was only preparing you for a day like this." The horse said to him: "And why should I not fall short, when you hand over my fodder to the grooms, and they wrong me and feed me only a little?" He said: "I give you Allah's covenant that after this day I will feed you only in my lap." At that, the horse charged and saved its rider. From then on, he fed it only in his lap, and his matter became famous among the people, and they began to come to him to hear this story. The news reached the King of the Romans, and he said: "No land is wronged where this man is." He schemed to bring him into his land. He sent to him a man from among the apostates who was with him. When he reached him, he showed him that his intention toward Islam and its people had become good, until he gained his trust. Then one day they went out walking along the shore, and [the apostate] had arranged with another person from the King of the Romans' side that they would help each other to capture him. When they flanked him to seize him, he raised his eyes to the sky and said: "O Allah, he deceived me only by means of You, so suffice me against them both with whatever You will." He said: So two lions came out toward them and seized them both, and the man returned safely. [Tarikh Dimashq (19/489, manuscript).]

* *

His saying (exalted is He): ﴿and makes you successors of the earth﴾ means: He causes one generation to succeed another before them, and one predecessor to be succeeded by another, as He says: ﴿If He wills, He will remove you and bring in after you whom He wills, just as He produced you from the offspring of another people﴾ [al-An'am: 133]; and He says: ﴿And it is He who made you successors on the earth and raised some of you above others in degrees﴾ [al-An'am: 165]; and He says: ﴿And when your Lord said to the angels, "Indeed, I will place upon the earth a successor (khalifa)"﴾ [al-Baqarah: 30], meaning a people some of whom succeed others, as we have already explained. Likewise in this verse: ﴿and makes you successors of the earth﴾, meaning a nation after a nation, a generation after a generation, and a people after a people. Had He willed, He would have brought them all into existence at one time, and not made some of them the offspring of others. Indeed, had He willed, He would have created them all together, just as He created Adam from dust. And had He willed to make some of them the offspring of others, but not caused anyone to die until the death of all occurred at one time, the earth would have become too narrow for them, and their livelihoods and earnings would have become too narrow for them, and some of them would have been harmed by others. But His wisdom and His power required that He create them from a single soul, then multiply them to the utmost extent, scatter them over the earth, and make them generations after generations and nations after nations, until the appointed term is complete and the created world is emptied, as He, blessed and exalted, has decreed, and as He has counted them and numbered them precisely. Then He will establish the Day of Resurrection and fully repay every doer for his deeds when the Book reaches its appointed term.

For this reason He says: ﴿Who answers the desperate one when he calls upon Him, and removes the evil, and makes you successors of the earth? Is there a god with Allah?﴾, meaning: is there anyone who has power over this? Or is there a god with Allah who is worshipped? It is already known that Allah is the One who alone does this. ﴿Little do you remember﴾, meaning: how little do they remember what would guide them to the truth and lead them to the straight path.

He says: ﴿Or who guides you in the darkness of the land and the sea?﴾ That is, by what He created of the heavenly and earthly signs, as He said: ﴿And landmarks; and by the star they are guided﴾ [An-Nahl: 16], and the Most High said: ﴿And it is He who placed for you the stars that you may be guided by them in the darknesses of the land and the sea﴾ [Al-An'am: 97], to the end of the verse.

﴿Or who sends the winds as good tidings before His mercy?﴾ That is, before the clouds that contain rain, by which He gives relief to His servants who are in drought, who have despaired. ﴿Is there a god with Allah? Exalted is Allah above what they associate with Him.﹀

That is, He is the One who, by His power and dominion, originates creation and then brings it back, as He said in another verse: ﴿Indeed, the seizure of your Lord is severe. Indeed, it is He who originates and repeats﴾ [Al-Buruj: 12, 13], and He said: ﴿And it is He who originates creation and then repeats it, and that is easier for Him﴾ [Ar-Rum: 27].

﴿And who provides for you from the heaven and the earth?﴾ That is, with what He sends down of rain from the sky and what He brings forth of the earth's blessings, as He said: ﴿By the sky of the returning rain, and by the earth of the splitting open﴾ [At-Tariq: 11, 12], and He said: ﴿He knows what enters into the earth and what comes out of it, and what descends from the sky and what ascends into it﴾ [Al-Hadid: 4]. So He, blessed and exalted, sends down from the sky blessed water and settles it in the earth, then brings forth by it [from it] [[Addition from F.]] kinds of crops, fruits, flowers, and other varied colors, ﴿Eat and graze your livestock. Indeed in that are signs for people of intellect﴾ [Ta-Ha: 54]. Therefore He said: ﴿Is there a god with Allah?﴾ That is, who did this? And according to the other reading: is he worshipped? ﴿Say, "Produce your proof"﴾ for the validity of what you claim of worshipping other gods, ﴿if you should be truthful﴾ in that. He knows that they have no argument and no proof, as Allah said: ﴿And whoever invokes with Allah another god, for which he has no proof, his account is only with his Lord. Indeed, the disbelievers will not succeed﴾ [Al-Mu'minun: 117].

**Commentary of Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Qur'an al-'Azim) on Surah 27, verses 65–66:**

Allah, exalted is He, says, commanding His Messenger ﷺ to say, as a teaching for all of creation: ﴿Say: None in the heavens and the earth knows the unseen, except Allah.﴾ His words ﴿except Allah﴾ are a disconnected exception (istithna' munqati', an exception not of the same category as what precedes it). That is, none knows this except Allah, exalted is He, for He alone is singular in this, with no partner. As He said: ﴿And with Him are the keys of the unseen; none knows them but He﴾ [al-An'am: 59], and He said: ﴿Indeed, Allah has knowledge of the Hour, and He sends down the rain, and He knows what is in the wombs. No soul knows what it will earn tomorrow, and no soul knows in what land it will die. Indeed, Allah is Knowing and Acquainted﴾ [Luqman: 34]. The verses on this are numerous.

* *

His words ﴿And they do not perceive when they will be resurrected﴾ mean: the creatures dwelling in the heavens and the earth do not perceive the time of the Hour, as He said: ﴿Its knowledge is burdensome in the heavens and the earth. It will not come to you except suddenly﴾ [al-A'raf: 187], meaning its knowledge is weighty upon the inhabitants of the heavens and the earth.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father narrated to us, 'Ali ibn al-Ja'd narrated to us, Abu Ja'far al-Razi narrated to us, from Dawud ibn Abi Hind, from al-Sha'bi, from Masruq, from 'Aishah (may Allah be pleased with her), who said: "Whoever claims that he knows what will happen tomorrow — meaning the Prophet ﷺ — has committed a great slander against Allah, for Allah, exalted is He, says: ﴿None in the heavens and the earth knows the unseen except Allah﴾"[[The origin of this is in the two Sahihs, but the evidence in them is the words of Allah, exalted is He: "And no soul knows what it will earn tomorrow," in place of this verse: "Say: None in the heavens knows..."]].

Qatadah said: Allah created these stars for three purposes: He made them an adornment for the sky, He made them a means of guidance, and He made them missiles against the devils. Whoever pursues anything else from them has spoken according to his own opinion, has missed his share, has wasted his portion, and has burdened himself with what he has no knowledge of. Indeed, some ignorant people concerning the command of Allah have invented from these stars a form of soothsaying: "Whoever marries under such and such a star, such and such will happen; whoever travels under such and such a star, such and such will happen; whoever is born under such and such a star, such and such will happen." By my life, there is no star under which the red and the black are not born, the short and the tall, the handsome and the ugly. The knowledge of this star, this creature, and this bird is not in any way knowledge of the unseen! Allah has decreed that none in the heavens and the earth knows the unseen except Allah, and they do not perceive when they will be resurrected.

Ibn Abi Hatim narrated it from him in these exact words, and it is a magnificent, firm, and sound statement.

* *

His words ﴿Rather, their knowledge has been exhausted concerning the Hereafter﴾ (bal idarak 'ilmuhum) mean: their knowledge has come to an end and has failed to know its time.

Others read it as "bal adraka 'ilmuhum," meaning: their knowledge in this matter has become equal (to that of others). This is as in Sahih Muslim, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to Jibril, when he asked him about the time of the Hour: "The one asked about it is no more knowing than the asker"[[Sahih Muslim, no. (8).]]. That is, the knowledge of the one asked and the asker is equal in their inability to attain knowledge of it.

'Ali ibn Abi Talhah narrated from Ibn 'Abbas: ﴿Rather, their knowledge has been exhausted concerning the Hereafter﴾ means: it has disappeared (ghaba).

Qatadah said: ﴿Rather, their knowledge has been exhausted concerning the Hereafter﴾ means: their Lord has made them ignorant. He says: knowledge of the Hereafter has not reached them. This is one opinion.

Ibn Jurayj narrated from 'Ata' al-Khurasani, from Ibn 'Abbas: "Rather, their knowledge has been exhausted concerning the Hereafter" — when knowledge no longer benefits. 'Ata' al-Khurasani and al-Suddi also said this: their knowledge is only attained and perfected on the Day of Resurrection, when it will no longer benefit them, as He said: ﴿How they will hear and see on the day they come to Us! But the wrongdoers today are in clear error﴾ [Maryam: 38].

Sufyan narrated from 'Amr ibn 'Ubayd, from al-Hasan, that he used to read: "Bal adraka 'ilmuhum," and said: their knowledge vanished in this world when they witnessed the Hereafter.

* *

His words ﴿Rather, they are in doubt concerning it﴾ refer to the category (of people), and the intended meaning is the disbelievers, as He said: ﴿And they will be presented before your Lord in rows: "You have come to Us as We created you the first time. But you claimed that We would not appoint for you a appointed time"﴾ [al-Kahf: 48], meaning: the disbelievers among you. Likewise, He says here: ﴿Rather, they are in doubt concerning it﴾, meaning: they doubt its existence and its occurrence. ﴿Rather, they are blind to it﴾, meaning: they are in great blindness and ignorance regarding its matter and its affair.

Allah says, informing about the polytheists who denied the Resurrection: they regarded as far-fetched the restoration of bodies after they had become bones, crumbled remains, and dust. Then He said: ﴿Indeed we have been promised this, we and our fathers before. This is nothing but the tales of the ancients.﴾ Meaning: we have been hearing of this, we and our fathers, and we see no reality or occurrence of it.

* *

Their saying: ﴿This is nothing but the tales of the ancients﴾ means: this promise of the restoration of bodies is nothing but the tales of the ancients, which a people took from those before them, one passing it on to another, and it has no reality.

Allah the Exalted answered them concerning what they supposed of disbelief and the denial of the Return, saying: ﴿Say﴾ — O Muhammad — to these people: ﴿Travel through the land and see how was the end of the criminals﴾, that is, those who denied the Messengers and what they brought of the matter of the Return and other things: how the vengeance of Allah, His punishment and His retribution befell them, and how Allah saved His noble Messengers and those believers who followed them from among them. This indicates the truthfulness and soundness of what the Messengers brought.

Then Allah the Exalted said, consoling His Prophet, may the blessings and peace of Allah be upon him: ﴿And do not grieve over them﴾, that is, over the deniers of what you have brought, and do not be distressed over them, nor let yourself go in sorrow over them, ﴿and do not be in distress because of what they plot﴾, that is, because of their scheming and their rejection of what you have brought. Indeed Allah will support you and aid you, and make your religion prevail over whoever opposes and defies it in the east and the west.

Ibn Kathir said, explaining Allah's words, informing about the polytheists' question concerning the Day of Resurrection and their denial that it would occur:

﴿And they say, "When is this promise, if you are truthful?"﴾ Allah replies to them: ﴿Say," O Muhammad, "Perhaps some of what you are seeking to hasten has drawn near to you."﴾ [Ibn 'Abbas said: "Perhaps it has come near," or "Perhaps it will be brought near to you," some of what you are seeking to hasten.] Likewise (Mujahid), al-Dahhak, 'Ata' al-Khurasani, Qatadah and al-Suddi said.

This is the meaning of His words: ﴿And they say, "When is it?" Say, "Perhaps it is near."﴾ [al-Isra': 51] And He said: ﴿They ask you to hasten the punishment, and indeed Hell will encompass the disbelievers.﴾ [al-'Ankabut: 54]

The lam (ل) entered into His words ﴿radifa lakum﴾ because it was taken to carry the meaning of "ajala lakum" (hastened for you), as Mujahid said in one narration from him: "﴿'Asa an yakuna radifa lakum﴾ means 'ajila lakum' (hastened for you)."

Then Allah said: ﴿And indeed, your Lord is full of bounty toward mankind﴾, meaning: in His bestowing His blessings upon them despite their wronging of themselves. Yet they do not thank Him for that, except for a few of them. ﴿And indeed, your Lord knows what their breasts conceal and what they declare.﴾ Meaning: He knows the hidden secrets and the inner thoughts, just as He knows the outward matters. ﴿Whether one of you conceals speech or openly declares it﴾ [al-Ra'd: 10]; ﴿He knows the secret and that which is yet more hidden﴾ [Ta-Ha: 7]; ﴿Unquestionably, when they cover themselves with their garments, He knows what they conceal and what they declare﴾ [Hud: 5].

Then Allah informed that He is the Knower of the unseen of the heavens and the earth, and that He is the Knower of the unseen and the witnessed, the unseen being what is hidden from the servants and what they have not witnessed. So He said: ﴿And there is not an unseen thing in the heaven or earth﴾. Ibn 'Abbas said: meaning, "there is not a thing," ﴿in the heaven or earth except that it is in a clear register.﴾ This is like His words: ﴿Do you not know that Allah knows what is in the heaven and the earth? Indeed, that is in a Book. Indeed, that for Allah is easy.﴾ [al-Hajj: 70]

Almighty Allah says, informing about His Mighty Book and what it contains of guidance, clear proofs, and criterion (in some manuscripts, "clarification"): **"Indeed, it relates to the Children of Israel, most of that about which they differ"** (they being the bearers of the Torah and the Gospel), such as their disagreement about Jesus and their divergence concerning him. The Jews fabricated falsehoods against him, and the Christians exaggerated regarding him. The Qur'an came to them with the moderate, true, and just statement: that he is a servant of Allah and one of His noble prophets and messengers, upon whom be the best of prayers and peace, as Allah says: **﴿That is Jesus, son of Mary, a statement of truth about which they dispute﴾** [Maryam 19:34].

And His saying: **﴿And indeed, it is guidance and mercy for the believers﴾** means: guidance for the hearts of the believers, and mercy for them in matters of practice.

Then He said: **﴿Indeed, your Lord will judge between them﴾**, i.e., on the Day of Resurrection, **﴿by His judgment, and He is the Mighty﴾** in His retribution, **﴿the Knowing﴾** of the deeds and words of His servants.

**﴿So rely upon Allah﴾**, i.e., in your affairs, and convey the message of your Lord. **﴿Indeed, you are upon the clear truth﴾**, i.e., you are upon the clear truth even if those who oppose you oppose you, from among those upon whom wretchedness has been decreed and upon whom the word of your Lord has come into effect, that they will not believe, even if every sign came to them. For this reason He said: **﴿Indeed, you cannot make the dead hear﴾**, i.e., you cannot make them hear anything that benefits them. Likewise these people have a covering over their hearts and deafness of disbelief in their ears. For this reason He said: **﴿Indeed, you cannot make the dead hear, nor can you make the deaf hear the call when they turn away, retreating. And you cannot guide the blind away from their error. You can only make hear those who believe in Our signs, so they are Muslims﴾** [i.e., in the sense that]: only one who is hearing and seeing will respond to you, the hearing and seeing that benefit the heart and insight, that submits to Allah, and to what came from Him through the tongues of the messengers, peace be upon them.

This beast will emerge at the end of time, when people have become corrupt, abandoned the commands of Allah, and altered the true religion. Allah will bring forth for them a beast from the earth. It has been said that it will come from Makkah, and it has been said that it will come from elsewhere, as its details will be explained later. It will speak to the people concerning this.

Ibn 'Abbas, al-Hasan and Qatadah said, and it is narrated from 'Ali, may Allah be pleased with him, that: "It will speak to them, meaning it will address them."

'Ata' al-Khurasani said: "It will speak to them, saying: 'Indeed the people were not certain of Our signs.'" This is narrated from 'Ali, and Ibn Jarir chose it. There is an obvious difficulty in this view, and Allah knows best.

Ibn 'Abbas, in one narration, said: "It will wound them." He also has another narration in which he said: "It does both, meaning this and that." This is a good view, and there is no contradiction, and Allah knows best.

Many hadiths and reports have been transmitted concerning the beast, so we will mention what is available of them, and Allah is the One sought for help.

Imam Ahmad said: Sufyan narrated to us, from Furat, from Abu al-Tufayl, from Hudhayfah ibn Asid al-Ghifari, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ looked down upon us from an upper room while we were discussing the matter of the Hour, and he said: "The Hour will not come until you see ten signs: the rising of the sun from its west, the smoke, the beast, the emergence of Ya'juj and Ma'juj, the coming down of 'Isa ibn Maryam, the Dajjal, and three eclipses: an eclipse in the west, an eclipse in the east, and an eclipse in the Arabian Peninsula; and a fire that will come out from the bottom of 'Adan, driving the people, or gathering the people; it will spend the night with them wherever they spend the night, and it will rest at midday with them wherever they rest." [Imam Ahmad narrated it in al-Musnad (4/6) but with differences in the wording; this wording is the context of the narration of Ibn Mahdi from Sufyan, and it is in al-Musnad (4/7).]

Muslim and the authors of the Sunan narrated the same in the same way, through several chains, from Furat al-Qazzaz, from Abu al-Tufayl 'Amir ibn Wathilah, from Hudhayfah, as a mawquf report (attributed to a Companion, not traced to the Prophet ﷺ). al-Tirmidhi said: "Hasan sahih." [Sahih Muslim no. (2901), Sunan Abi Dawud no. (4311), Sunan al-Tirmidhi no. (2183), Sunan Ibn Majah no. (4041).] Muslim also narrated it from the hadith of 'Abd al-'Aziz ibn Rufay', from Abu al-Tufayl, from him, as a marfu' report (traced to the Prophet ﷺ). [Sahih Muslim no. (2901).] And Allah knows best.

Another chain: Abu Dawud al-Tayalisi said, from Talhah ibn 'Amr and Jarir ibn Hazim. As for Talhah, he said: 'Abd Allah ibn 'Ubayd Allah ibn 'Umayr al-Laythi informed me that Abu al-Tufayl narrated to him, from Hudhayfah ibn Asid al-Ghifari, Abu Sarihah. As for Jarir, he said: from 'Abd Allah ibn 'Ubayd, from a man from the family of 'Abd Allah ibn Mas'ud. The hadith of Talhah is more complete and better. He said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ mentioned the beast and said: "It has three emergences during the ages. It will emerge once from the furthest desert, and its mention will not enter the town, meaning Makkah. Then it will remain hidden for a long time, then it will emerge a second time, less than that, and its mention will spread among the people of the desert, and its mention will enter the town," meaning Makkah. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Then, while the people are in the greatest mosque in the sight of Allah in sanctity and honour, the Masjid al-Haram, it will surprise them only while it is roaring between the Corner (al-Rukn) and the Station (al-Maqam), shaking the dust from its head. The people will scatter from it, some in groups and some together, and a remnant of the believers will remain, and they will know that they have not escaped Allah. Then it will begin with them and mark their faces until it makes them like a shining star, and it will go away in the earth, no seeker will overtake it, and no fleeing one will escape from it. Even a man will seek refuge from it in prayer, and it will come to him from behind and say: 'O so-and-so, are you praying now?' He will turn to it, and it will mark him on his face. Then it will depart, and the people will share in their wealth, and they will travel together in the cities. The believer will be recognised from the disbeliever, until the believer says: 'O disbeliever, pay me my right!' And until the disbeliever says: 'O believer, pay me my right!'" [Musnad al-Tayalisi no. (1069).]

Ibn Jarir narrated it through two chains, from Hudhayfah ibn Asid as a mawquf report, and Allah knows best. He also narrated it from the narration of Hudhayfah ibn al-Yaman as a marfu' report, and that this happens in the time of 'Isa ibn Maryam, while he is circumambulating the House; but its chain is not sound. [Tafsir al-Tabari (20/10), (20/11).]

Another hadith: Muslim ibn al-Hajjaj said: Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah narrated to us, Muhammad ibn Bishr narrated to us, from Abu Hayyan, from Abu Zur'ah, from 'Abd Allah ibn 'Amr, who said: I memorised from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ a hadith that I have not forgotten since: I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: "Indeed the first of the signs to emerge is the rising of the sun from its west, and the emergence of the beast before the people in the forenoon; whichever of the two is before the other, the other will follow it closely." [Sahih Muslim no. (2941).]

Another hadith: Muslim narrated in his Sahih, from the hadith of al-'Ala' ibn 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Ya'qub, the freed slave of al-Huraqah, from his father, from Abu Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Hasten to good deeds before six: the rising of the sun from its west, or the smoke, or the Dajjal, or the beast, or the matter of one of you personally, or the matter of the common people." [Sahih Muslim no. (2947).] He also has, from the hadith of Qatadah, from al-Hasan, from Ziyad ibn Rabah, from Abu Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him, from the Prophet ﷺ, who said: "Hasten to good deeds before six: the Dajjal, the smoke, the beast of the earth, the rising of the sun from its west, the matter of the common people, and the special matter of one of you." [Sahih Muslim no. (2947).]

Another hadith: Ibn Majah said: Harmalah ibn Yahya narrated to us, Ibn Wahb narrated to us, 'Amr ibn al-Harith and Ibn Lahi'ah informed me, from Yazid ibn Abi Habib, from Sinan ibn Sa'd, from Anas ibn Malik, may Allah be pleased with him, from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, who said: "Hasten to good deeds before six: the rising of the sun from its west, the smoke, the beast of the earth, the Dajjal, the special matter of one of you, and the matter of the common people." He alone narrated it. [Sunan Ibn Majah no. (4056). al-Busiri said in al-Zawa'id (3/256): "This is a hasan chain; Sinan ibn Sa'd is disputed, and his name is disputed."]

Another hadith: Abu Dawud al-Tayalisi also said: Hammad ibn Salamah narrated to us, from 'Ali ibn Zayd, from Aws [in ha, fa, and alif: "Uways"; the affirmed reading is from the Musnad] ibn Khalid, from Abu Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "The beast of the earth will emerge, and with it will be the staff of Musa and the seal of Sulayman, peace be upon them both. It will strike the nose of the disbeliever with the staff, and it will make the face of the believer shine with the seal, until the people gather at the same table, and the believer is recognised from the disbeliever."

Imam Ahmad also narrated it, from Bahz, 'Affan and Yazid ibn Harun, all three from Hammad ibn Salamah, with the same chain. [Musnad al-Tayalisi no. (2564); al-Musnad (2/295) from the narration of 'Affan and Yazid, and (2/291) from the narration of Bahz.] He said: "It will strike the nose of the disbeliever with the seal, and it will make the face of the believer shine with the staff, until the people of a single table gather, and this one says: 'O believer!' and that one says: 'O disbeliever!'"

Ibn Majah also narrated it, from Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah, from Yunus ibn Muhammad al-Mu'addib, from Hammad ibn Salamah, with the same chain. [Sunan Ibn Majah no. (4066).]

Another hadith: Ibn Majah said: Abu Ghassan Muhammad ibn 'Amr narrated to us, Abu Tumaylah narrated to us, Khalid ibn 'Ubayd narrated to us, 'Abd Allah ibn Buraydah narrated to us, from his father, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ took me to a place in the desert, near Makkah, and there was dry land around it with sand. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "The beast will emerge from this place," and suddenly there was a crack of a span.

Ibn Buraydah said: Years after that I performed Hajj, and he showed us a staff of his, and it was like this staff of mine, such-and-such. [Sunan Ibn Majah no. (4067). al-Busiri said in al-Zawa'id (3/259): "This is a weak chain."]

'Abd al-Razzaq said, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah, that Ibn 'Abbas said: It is a beast with fine down, having four legs, that emerges from some of the valleys of Tihamah. [Tafsir 'Abd al-Razzaq (2/71).]

Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father narrated to us, 'Abd Allah ibn Raja' narrated to us, Fudayl ibn Marzuq narrated to us, from 'Atiyyah, who said: 'Abd Allah said: The beast will emerge from a crack in al-Safa, like the running of a horse, for three days, and a third of it will not have emerged.

Muhammad ibn Ishaq said, from Aban ibn Salih, who said: 'Abd Allah ibn 'Amr was asked about the beast, and he said: The beast emerges from beneath a rock at Jiyad. By Allah, if I were with them, or if I wished, I would strike with my staff the rock from beneath which the beast emerges. It was said: What will it do, O 'Abd Allah ibn 'Amr? He said: It will face the east and cry out a cry that will pierce through it, then it will face Syria and cry out a cry that will pierce through it, then it will face the west and cry out a cry that will pierce through it, then it will face Yemen and cry out a cry that will pierce through it, then it will go out from Makkah and reach 'Usfan in the morning. It was said: Then what? He said: I do not know.

From 'Abd Allah ibn 'Umar, that he said: The beast will emerge on the night of Jam' (Muzdalifah). [Ibn Abi Shaybah narrated it in al-Musannaf (15/180) through 'Abd al-Malik ibn al-Mughirah, from Ibn al-Baylaman, from Ibn 'Umar, who said: "The beast will emerge on the night of Jam' while the people are travelling to Mina, and it will carry them between its rump and its tail, and no hypocrite will remain except that it will mark him, and it will wipe the believer." He said: "They will wake in the morning and they will be more evil than the Dajjal."] Ibn Abi Hatim also narrated it, and its chain includes Ibn al-Baylaman.

From Wahb ibn Munabbih: that he related from the speech of 'Uzayr, peace be upon him, that he said: "And a beast will emerge from beneath Sodom, speaking to the people, and everyone will hear it, and it will cause pregnant women to give birth before completion, and sweet water will turn salty, and friends will become enemies, and wisdom will be burned, and knowledge will be lifted, and the earth nearest to it will speak. In that time people will hope for what they will not reach, will toil for what they will not attain, and will work for what they will not eat." Ibn Abi Hatim narrated it from him.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father narrated to us, Abu Salih, scribe of al-Layth, narrated to us, Mu'awiyah ibn Salih narrated to me, from Abu Maryam, that he heard Abu Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him, say: Indeed the beast has from every colour, and the distance between its two horns is a farsakh (about three miles) for the rider.

Ibn 'Abbas said: It is like a large spear.

From the Commander of the Faithful, 'Ali ibn Abi Talib, may Allah be pleased with him, that he said: "It is a beast that has feathers, down and a hoof, and it has no tail, and it has a beard, and it will bring forth three times the speed of a noble horse, and a third of it has not emerged." [In f: "two-thirds" in the variant reading.] Ibn Abi Hatim narrated it.

Ibn Jurayj said, from Ibn al-Zubayr, that he described the beast, saying: "Its head is the head of a bull, its eye is the eye of a pig, its ear is the ear of an elephant, its horn is the horn of a stag (ayyal), its neck is the neck of an ostrich, its chest is the chest of a lion, its color is the color of a tiger (nimr), its flank is the flank of a cat, its tail is the tail of a ram, and its legs are the legs of a camel. Between each two joints there are twelve [cubits] (dhira'an). With it will come the staff of Musa and the ring of Sulayman. No believer will remain except that it will strike on his face a white spot with the staff of Musa, and that spot will spread until his face becomes white by it. And no disbeliever will remain except that it will strike on his face a black spot with the ring of Sulayman, and that spot will spread until his face becomes black by it, so much so that people will trade in the markets, saying: 'How much is this, O believer? How much is this, O disbeliever?' And so much so that the people of a household will sit at their table, and they will know their believer from their disbeliever. Then the beast will say to them: 'O so-and-so, rejoice, you are among the people of Paradise; and O so-and-so, you are among the people of the Fire.'" That is the saying of Allah the Exalted: ﴿And when the word is fulfilled against them, We will bring forth for them a creature from the earth, speaking to them that mankind did not have certainty in Our verses.﴾ [[This is from the Isra'iliyyat, and there is no benefit in mentioning it, and the descriptions of the beast are known only to Allah the Exalted.]]

Ibn Kathir said, reporting from the Exalted about the Day of Resurrection and the gathering of the wrongdoers who denied God's signs and His messengers before God, Mighty and Majestic, so that He might question them about what they did in the worldly abode, as rebuke, reproach, belittlement and humiliation. He said: ﴿And on the Day We gather from every nation a company of those who denied Our signs, then they will be driven in order﴾. That is, from every people and every generation a group (fawj), i.e., a company. As He, the Exalted, said: ﴿Assemble those who did wrong and their companions﴾ [As-Saffat 37:22], and He, the Exalted, said: ﴿And when the souls are paired﴾ [At-Takwir 81:7].

As for His words ﴿then they will be driven in order﴾, Ibn Abbas, may Allah be pleased with him and his father, said: they will be pushed. Qatadah said: guards (wazaʿah) will turn back their first on to their last. Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd ibn Aslam said: they will be driven.

﴿Until, when they arrive﴾, that is, they will be made to stand before Allah, Mighty and Majestic, at the place of questioning. ﴿He will say: "Did you deny My signs without comprehending them in knowledge, or what was it that you used to do?"﴾ That is, they will be questioned about their beliefs and their deeds. Since they were not among the people of happiness, and were as Allah, the Exalted, said of them: ﴿So he neither believed nor prayed, but denied and turned away﴾ [Al-Qiyamah 75:31-32], then the proof (hujjah) was established against them, and they had no excuse by which to plead. As He, the Exalted, said: ﴿This is a Day when they will not speak, nor will they be permitted to make excuse. Woe that Day to the deniers﴾ [Al-Mursalat 77:35-37]. Likewise He said here: ﴿And the word will fall upon them because of their wrongdoing, and they will not speak﴾. That is, they will be struck dumb, so they will have no answer, because in the worldly abode they were wrongdoers against themselves, and they have been returned to the Knower of the unseen and the witnessed, from Whom no hidden thing is concealed.

Then the Exalted said, drawing attention to His complete power, His great sovereignty and His exalted majesty, whose command must be obeyed and whose orders must be followed, and to the truthfulness of His prophets in what they brought of the truth from which there is no escape, saying: ﴿Do they not see that We made the night for them to rest therein﴾, that is, in it is darkness by which their movements come to rest, their breaths grow still, and they are relieved of the fatigue of toil in their day. ﴿And the day giving sight﴾, that is, bright and illuminating, and by means of it they go about their livelihoods, gains, journeys, trade, and other affairs they need. ﴿Surely in that are signs for a people who believe﴾.

Ibn Kathir (may Allah have mercy on him) says:

Allah, exalted is He, informs us about the terror of the Day of the blowing of the Trumpet (nafkhat al-faza'), and it is as has come in the hadith: "A horn into which it is blown." In the hadith about the Trumpet (al-Sur), Israfil is the one who blows into it by the command of Allah, exalted is He. He first blows the blast of terror and prolongs it. This happens at the end of the life of this world, when the Hour comes upon the most wicked of the living, and whoever is in the heavens and whoever is on the earth is terrified, ﴿except whom Allah wills﴾. They are the martyrs, for they are alive with their Lord, being provided for.

Imam Muslim ibn al-Hajjaj said: Ubayd Allah ibn Mu'adh al-'Anbari narrated to us, my father narrated to us, Shu'bah narrated to us, from al-Nu'man ibn Salim: I heard Ya'qub ibn 'Asim ibn 'Urwah ibn Mas'ud al-Thaqafi say: I heard 'Abd Allah ibn 'Amr, may Allah be pleased with him, and a man came to him and said: "What is this hadith that you narrate, that the Hour will come at such and such?" He said: "Subhan Allah, or: La ilaha illa Allah, or a word similar to them. I had resolved not to narrate anything to anyone ever again. I only said: 'You will soon see a great matter that will ruin the House, and such and such will happen.'" Then he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "The Dajjal will emerge among my ummah and remain forty -[I do not know whether forty] days, or forty months, or forty years- then Allah will send 'Isa ibn Maryam, who will look like 'Urwah ibn Mas'ud, and he will seek him out and destroy him. Then the people will remain seven years with no enmity between any two people. Then Allah will send a cold wind from the direction of al-Sham, and there will not remain on the face of the earth anyone who has in his heart even an atom's weight of good or faith, except that it will take him, until if one of them entered into the core of a mountain, it would enter after him and seize him." He said: "I heard it from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, who said: 'Then the most wicked of people will remain, with the lightness of birds and the minds of beasts, not recognising good nor denouncing evil. Then Satan will appear to them and say: Will you not respond? They will say: What do you command us? So he will command them to worship idols, and in that state their provision will be abundant and their life good. Then the Trumpet will be blown, and no one who hears it will fail to incline his neck (asghā laytan)...'" He said: "The first to hear it will be a man repairing the watering-trough of his camels." He said: "So he will swoon, and the people will swoon. Then Allah will send down, or He said: He will bring down, rain like the tal, or he said: the zill, Nu'man being doubtful, and from it the bodies of the people will grow. Then it will be blown into again, and behold, they will be standing, looking. Then it will be said: O people, come to your Lord, and stop them, for they are to be questioned. Then it will be said: Bring out the portion of the Fire. It will be asked: From how many? It will be said: From every thousand, nine hundred and ninety-nine." He said: "That is the day that will make the children grey-haired, and that is the day when a shin will be uncovered."

[Sahih Muslim, no. 2940.]

* *

As for His saying: "Then the Trumpet is blown, and none who is in the heavens or the earth will hear it except that he inclines his neck (liyt)": al-layt is the side of the neck, meaning he inclines his neck to listen well to it from the sky.

This is the blast of terror. Then after that is the blast of swooning (nafkhat al-sa'q), which is death. Then after that is the blast of standing up before the Lord of the worlds, which is the resurrection from the graves for all creatures. Therefore He said: ﴿And all will come to Him humbled﴾. It is read with a long vowel (kullun) and without it, as a verb (atawhu), with the same meaning. ﴿Humbled (dakhirin)﴾ means subdued and obedient, none of them failing to comply with His command, as Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿On the Day He calls you, and you will respond with His praise﴾ [al-Isra' 52], and He said: ﴿Then when He calls you with a single call from the earth, behold, you will come forth﴾ [al-Rum 25].

In the hadith about the Trumpet, it is related that at the third blast, Allah commands the souls, and they are placed in a hole in the Trumpet. Then Israfil blows into it after the bodies have grown in their graves and places. When the Trumpet is blown, the souls fly out: the souls of the believers shine with light, and the souls of the disbelievers are dark. Allah, Mighty and Majestic, says: "By My might and My majesty, every soul will surely return to its body." So the souls come to their bodies, and they spread through them as poison spreads through the one who has been stung. Then they rise and shake the dust from their graves. Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿On the Day they come forth from the graves swiftly, as if they were rushing to a target﴾ [al-Ma'arij 43].

* *

As for His saying: ﴿And you see the mountains, you think them fixed, while they pass away like the passing of clouds﴾: you see them as if they were firm and remaining as they were, while they pass like clouds, that is, they leave their places, as Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿On the Day the sky will sway violently and the mountains will move swiftly﴾ [al-Tur 9-10], and He said: ﴿They ask you about the mountains; say: My Lord will scatter them as dust, and leave them as a level plain, in which you will see no crookedness or elevation﴾ [Ta-Ha 105-107], and Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿On the Day We set the mountains in motion and you see the earth laid bare﴾ [al-Kahf 47].

* *

As for His saying: ﴿The handiwork of Allah, who has perfected everything﴾: that is, He does that by His great power, who has perfected all that He created and placed in it of wisdom what He placed. ﴿Indeed, He is Aware of what you do﴾: that is, He knows what His servants do of good and evil, and will recompense them for it.

Then Allah explained the state of the blessed and the wretched on that day, saying: ﴿Whoever brings a good deed will have better than it﴾. Qatadah said: that means sincerity (al-ikhlas). Zayn al-'Abidin said: it is "La ilaha illa Allah". And it has been made clear in another place that he will have ten times its like (Ibn Kathir, may Allah have mercy on him, refers to verse 160 of Surah al-An'am: ﴿Whoever brings a good deed will have ten times its like, and whoever brings an evil deed will not be recompensed except with its like, and they will not be wronged﴾). ﴿And they will be safe from the terror of that Day﴾, as He said in another verse: ﴿The greatest terror will not grieve them﴾ [al-Anbiya' 103], and He said: ﴿Is one who is thrown into the Fire better, or one who comes safe on the Day of Resurrection?﴾ [Fussilat 40], and He said: ﴿And they will be secure in the lofty chambers﴾ [Saba' 37].

* *

As for His saying: ﴿And whoever brings an evil deed, their faces will be thrown into the Fire﴾: that is, whoever meets Allah as an evildoer with no good deed, or whose evil deeds outweigh his good deeds, each according to his measure. Therefore He said: ﴿Are you recompensed except for what you used to do?﴾

Ibn Mas'ud, Abu Hurayrah, Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them, Anas ibn Malik, 'Ata', Sa'id ibn Jubayr, 'Ikrimah, Mujahid, Ibrahim al-Nakha'i, Abu Wa'il, Abu Salih, Muhammad ibn Ka'b, Zayd ibn Aslam, al-Zuhri, al-Suddi, al-Dahhak, al-Hasan, Qatadah, and Ibn Zayd said, regarding His saying ﴿And whoever brings an evil deed﴾: meaning, with polytheism (shirk).

His saying ﴿and that I recite the Qur'an﴾ means: to the people, conveying it to them, just as He said: ﴿That We recite to you of the signs and the wise reminder﴾ [Al 'Imran: 58], and as He said: ﴿We recite to you some of the news of Musa and Fir'awn in truth for a people who believe﴾ [al-Qasas: 3]. Meaning: I am only a conveyer and a warner. ﴿So whoever is guided, he is guided only for himself; and whoever strays, say, "I am only among the warners"﴾, meaning: I have the same standing as the messengers who warned their peoples, who fulfilled what was upon them of conveying the message to them, and were freed of their obligation, while the reckoning of their nations is with Allah, just as He said: ﴿So upon you is only the conveying, and upon Us is the reckoning﴾ [al-Ra'd: 40], and He said: ﴿You are only a warner, and Allah is Disposer of all things﴾ [Hud: 12].

﴿And say, "Praise is for Allah; He will show you His signs, and you will recognise them"﴾, meaning: Praise is for Allah, who does not punish anyone except after the establishment of proof against him and the giving of warning to him. Therefore He said: ﴿He will show you His signs, and you will recognise them﴾, just as Allah the Exalted said: ﴿We will show them Our signs in the horizons and within themselves until it becomes clear to them that it is the truth﴾ [Fussilat: 53].

* *

His saying ﴿And your Lord is not unaware of what you do﴾ means: rather, He is Witness over everything.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: It was mentioned from Abu 'Umar al-Hawdi Hafs ibn 'Umar: Abu Umayya ibn Ya'la al-Thaqafi narrated to us, Sa'id ibn Abi Sa'id narrated to us, I heard Abu Hurayrah say: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "O people, let none of you be deceived concerning Allah; for if Allah were heedless of anything, He would be heedless of the gnat, the mustard seed and the ant" [Narrated by al-Daylami in Musnad al-Firdaws, no. 8167, through the chain of Abu Umayya ibn Ya'la.]

[He also said:] Muhammad ibn Yahya narrated to us, Nasr ibn 'Ali narrated to us, my father said: Khalid ibn Qays informed me, from Matar, from 'Umar ibn 'Abd al-'Aziz who said: "If Allah were heedless of anything, He would be heedless of what the winds efface of the footprints of the son of Adam."

It is also mentioned from Imam Ahmad, may Allah have mercy on him, that he used to recite these two verses, whether they were his or someone else's:

If you are ever alone in a time, do not say, "I am alone," but say, "a Watcher is over me."
And do not think that Allah is heedless for an hour, nor that what is hidden from Him is absent.

Allah, exalted is He, says, informing His Messenger and commanding him to say: ﴿Indeed, I have been commanded to worship the Lord of this city, who has made it sacred, and to Him belongs everything﴾, just as He said: ﴿Say, "O mankind, if you are in doubt about my religion, then I do not worship those you worship besides Allah, but I worship Allah, who causes you to die"﴾ [Yunus: 104].

The attribution of lordship to the city is for the sake of honouring it and showing care for it, just as He said: ﴿So let them worship the Lord of this House, who has fed them against hunger and made them safe from fear﴾ [Quraysh: 3, 4].

* *

His saying ﴿who has made it sacred﴾ means: He who made it sacred, both by decree and by law, through His making it sacred, as is established in the Two Sahihs from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said on the day of the Conquest of Makkah: "Indeed, this city was made sacred by Allah on the day He created the heavens and the earth, so it is sacred by the sanctity of Allah until the Day of Resurrection. Its thorny plants may not be cut, its game may not be chased, its lost property may not be picked up except by one who announces it, and its grass may not be cut..." and the hadith in full. It is also established in the Sahihs, the Hasan collections and the Musnads through many chains that yield certainty, as is explained in its proper place in the Book of Rulings, and to Allah belongs all praise.
